verses.1:1: The words of Nehemiah son of Hacaliah. It came about in the month of Kislev, in the twentieth year, when I was in Susa the citadel,
verses.1:2: that Hanani, one of my brothers, arrived—he and men from Judah—and I asked them about the Jews, the escaped remnant who were left from the captivity, and about Jerusalem.
verses.1:3: They said to me, "The remnant who are left from the captivity there in the province are in great distress and in reproach, and the wall of Jerusalem is broken down, and its gates have been burned with fire."
verses.1:4: When I heard these words, I sat down and wept, and I mourned for days; and I continued fasting and praying before the God of heaven.
verses.1:5: And I said, "Please, LORD, God of heaven, the great and awesome God, who keeps the covenant and loyal love for those who love Him and keep His commandments:
verses.1:6: let Your ear please be attentive and Your eyes open to listen to the prayer of Your servant, which I am praying before You today, day and night, on behalf of the sons of Israel, Your servants, while confessing the sins of the sons of Israel that we have sinned against You. Both I and my father's house have sinned.
verses.1:7: We have indeed acted corruptly against You, and we have not kept the commandments, the statutes, and the ordinances that You commanded Your servant Moses.
verses.1:8: Please remember the word that You commanded Your servant Moses, saying, 'If you act unfaithfully, I will scatter you among the peoples;
verses.1:9: but if you return to Me and keep My commandments and do them, even if your outcasts are at the end of the heavens, from there I will gather them and bring them to the place that I have chosen to make My name dwell there.'
verses.1:10: Now they are Your servants and Your people, whom You redeemed by Your great power and by Your strong hand.
verses.1:11: Please, Lord, let Your ear be attentive to the prayer of Your servant and to the prayer of Your servants who take delight in fearing Your name; and please grant success to Your servant today, and grant him compassion before this man." Now I was cupbearer to the king.
verses.2:1: It came about in the month of Nisan, in the twentieth year of King Artaxerxes, when wine was before him, that I took up the wine and gave it to the king. Now I had not been sad in his presence.
verses.2:2: So the king said to me, "Why is your face sad, though you are not sick? This is nothing other than sadness of heart." Then I was very much afraid.
verses.2:3: I said to the king, "May the king live forever! Why should my face not be sad, when the city, the place of my fathers' tombs, lies desolate, and its gates have been consumed by fire?"
verses.2:4: Then the king said to me, "What is it that you are requesting?" So I prayed to the God of heaven.
verses.2:5: And I said to the king, "If it seems good to the king, and if your servant is pleasing before you, send me to Judah, to the city of my fathers' tombs, that I may rebuild it."
verses.2:6: Then the king said to me—with the queen sitting beside him—"How long will your journey be, and when will you return?" So it pleased the king to send me, and I gave him a set time.
verses.2:7: And I said to the king, "If it seems good to the king, let letters be given to me for the governors of Beyond the River, that they may let me pass through until I arrive in Judah,
verses.2:8: and a letter to Asaph, the keeper of the king's forest, that he may give me timber to lay beams for the gates of the citadel belonging to the temple, and for the wall of the city, and for the house that I will enter." And the king granted them to me, according to the good hand of my God upon me.
verses.2:9: Then I came to the governors of Beyond the River and gave them the king's letters. Now the king had sent army officers and horsemen with me.
verses.2:10: When Sanballat the Horonite and Tobiah the Ammonite servant heard of it, it was greatly displeasing to them that a man had come to seek the good of the sons of Israel.
verses.2:11: So I came to Jerusalem and was there three days.
verses.2:12: Then I arose in the night, I and a few men with me; and I did not tell anyone what my God was putting into my heart to do for Jerusalem. And there was no animal with me except the animal on which I was riding.
verses.2:13: So I went out by the Valley Gate at night, toward the front of the Dragon Spring and to the Dung Gate; and I was inspecting the walls of Jerusalem, which were broken down, and its gates had been consumed by fire.
verses.2:14: Then I passed on to the Fountain Gate and to the King's Pool, but there was no room for the animal under me to pass.
verses.2:15: So I went up along the valley at night and continued inspecting the wall; then I turned back, entered through the Valley Gate, and returned.
verses.2:16: And the officials did not know where I had gone or what I was doing, nor had I yet told the Jews, the priests, the nobles, the officials, or the rest of those doing the work.
verses.2:17: Then I said to them, "You see the distress we are in, how Jerusalem lies desolate and its gates are burned with fire. Come, let us rebuild the wall of Jerusalem, so that we may no longer be a reproach."
verses.2:18: And I told them about the hand of my God, which had been good upon me, and also the king's words that he had spoken to me. And they said, "Let us arise and build." So they strengthened their hands for the good cause.
verses.2:19: But when Sanballat the Horonite, Tobiah the Ammonite servant, and Geshem the Arab heard of it, they mocked us and despised us, and said, "What is this thing that you are doing? Are you rebelling against the king?"
verses.2:20: So I gave them an answer and said to them, "The God of heaven—He will grant us success, and we, His servants, will arise and build; but as for you, you have no portion, right, or memorial in Jerusalem."
verses.3:1: Then Eliashib the high priest arose with his brothers the priests, and they built the Sheep Gate. They consecrated it and set up its doors; they consecrated it as far as the Tower of the Hundred, as far as the Tower of Hananel.
verses.3:2: And next to him the men of Jericho built. And next to him Zaccur son of Imri built.
verses.3:3: Now the sons of Hassenaah built the Fish Gate; they laid its beams and set up its doors, its bolts, and its bars.
verses.3:4: Next to them Meremoth son of Uriah, son of Hakkoz, made repairs. Next to them Meshullam son of Berechiah, son of Meshezabel, made repairs. Next to them Zadok son of Baana made repairs.
verses.3:5: Next to them the Tekoites made repairs, but their nobles did not put their necks to the work of their lords.
verses.3:6: Joiada son of Paseah and Meshullam son of Besodeiah repaired the Old Gate; they laid its beams and set up its doors, its bolts, and its bars.
verses.3:8: Next to him Uzziel son of Harhaiah, of the goldsmiths, made repairs. And next to him Hananiah, one of the perfumers, made repairs; and they restored Jerusalem as far as the Broad Wall.
verses.3:9: Next to them Rephaiah son of Hur, ruler of half the district of Jerusalem, made repairs.
verses.3:10: Next to them Jedaiah son of Harumaph made repairs, even opposite his house. And next to him Hattush son of Hashabneiah made repairs.
verses.3:11: Malchijah son of Harim and Hasshub son of Pahath-moab repaired another section and the Tower of the Ovens.
verses.3:12: Next to him Shallum son of Hallohesh, ruler of half the district of Jerusalem, made repairs—he and his daughters.
verses.3:13: Hanun and the inhabitants of Zanoah repaired the Valley Gate; they built it and set up its doors, its bolts, and its bars, along with a thousand cubits of the wall as far as the Dung Gate.
verses.3:14: Malchijah son of Rechab, ruler of the district of Beth-haccherem, repaired the Dung Gate; he built it and set up its doors, its bolts, and its bars.
verses.3:15: Shallun son of Col-hozeh, ruler of the district of Mizpah, repaired the Fountain Gate; he built it, roofed it, and set up its doors, its bolts, and its bars. He also repaired the wall of the Pool of Shelah by the king's garden, as far as the stairs that go down from the City of David.
verses.3:16: After him Nehemiah son of Azbuk, ruler of half the district of Beth-zur, made repairs to a point opposite the tombs of David, and as far as the constructed pool, and as far as the House of the Mighty Men.
verses.3:17: After him the Levites made repairs: Rehum son of Bani. Next to him Hashabiah, ruler of half the district of Keilah, made repairs for his district.
verses.3:18: After him their brothers made repairs: Bavvai son of Henadad, ruler of half the district of Keilah.
verses.3:19: Next to him Ezer son of Jeshua, ruler of Mizpah, repaired another section opposite the ascent to the armory at the Angle.
verses.3:20: After him Baruch son of Zaccai zealously repaired another section, from the Angle to the doorway of the house of Eliashib the high priest.
verses.3:21: After him Meremoth son of Uriah, son of Hakkoz, repaired another section, from the doorway of the house of Eliashib to the end of the house of Eliashib.
verses.3:22: After him the priests, the men of the plain, made repairs.
verses.3:23: After him Benjamin and Hasshub made repairs opposite their house. After him Azariah son of Maaseiah, son of Ananiah, made repairs beside his house.
verses.3:24: After him Binnui son of Henadad repaired another section, from the house of Azariah to the Angle and to the Corner.
verses.3:25: Palal son of Uzai made repairs opposite the Angle and the tower projecting from the upper house of the king, which is by the court of the guard. After him Pedaiah son of Parosh made repairs.
verses.3:26: Now the temple servants were dwelling on Ophel, as far as a point opposite the Water Gate on the east and the projecting tower.
verses.3:27: After him the Tekoites repaired another section, from opposite the great projecting tower to the wall of Ophel.
verses.3:28: Above the Horse Gate the priests made repairs, each one opposite his house.
verses.3:29: After him Zadok son of Immer made repairs opposite his house. And after him Shemaiah son of Shecaniah, the keeper of the East Gate, made repairs.
verses.3:30: After him Hananiah son of Shelemiah and Hanun, the sixth son of Zalaph, repaired another section. After him Meshullam son of Berechiah made repairs opposite his chamber.
verses.3:31: After him Malchijah, one of the goldsmiths, made repairs as far as the house of the temple servants and of the merchants, opposite the Inspection Gate, and as far as the upper chamber of the Corner.
verses.3:32: And between the upper chamber of the Corner and the Sheep Gate, the goldsmiths and the merchants made repairs.
verses.3:33: Now when Sanballat heard that we were building the wall, he burned with anger and was greatly indignant, and he mocked the Jews.
verses.3:34: And he spoke before his brothers and the army of Samaria, and said, "What are the feeble Jews doing? Will they restore it for themselves? Will they offer sacrifices? Will they finish in a day? Will they revive the stones from the heaps of dust, burned as they are?"
verses.3:35: Now Tobiah the Ammonite was beside him, and he said, "Even what they are building—if a fox goes up on it, it will break down their stone wall!"
verses.3:36: Hear, our God, for we have become an object of contempt; turn back their reproach upon their own head, and give them over as plunder in a land of captivity.
verses.3:37: Do not cover their iniquity, and do not let their sin be blotted out from before You, for they have provoked anger in front of the builders.
verses.4:1: Now when Sanballat, Tobiah, the Arabs, the Ammonites, and the Ashdodites heard that repair was going forward on the walls of Jerusalem, that the breaches had begun to be closed up, they became very angry.
verses.4:2: All of them conspired together to come and fight against Jerusalem and to cause confusion in it.
verses.4:3: Yet we prayed to our God, and we stationed a guard against them day and night on account of them.
verses.4:4: Then Judah said, "The strength of the burden-bearer has faltered, and there is much rubble, and we are not able to build on the wall."
verses.4:5: And our adversaries said, "They will not know and will not see until we come into their midst and kill them and make the work cease."
verses.4:6: Now when the Jews who lived beside them came, they told us ten times from all the places, "You must return to us."
verses.4:7: So I stationed the people in the lowest parts of the space behind the wall, in the exposed places—I stationed them by families, with their swords, their spears, and their bows.
verses.4:8: Then I looked, and I rose and said to the nobles, to the officials, and to the rest of the people, "Do not fear them! Remember the great and awesome Lord, and fight for your brothers, your sons and your daughters, your wives and your houses."
verses.4:9: Now when our enemies heard that it was known to us and that God had thwarted their plan, all of us returned to the wall, each man to his work.
verses.4:10: From that day on, half of my attendants were doing the work while half of them held the spears, the shields, the bows, and the coats of mail, and the leaders were behind the entire house of Judah.
verses.4:11: Those who were building on the wall and those who were carrying burdens were loading up: with one hand each was doing the work, and the other held a weapon.
verses.4:12: And as for the builders, each man had his sword strapped to his waist as they built; and the one who blew the ram's horn was beside me.
verses.4:13: And I said to the nobles, to the officials, and to the rest of the people, "The work is great and extensive, and we are separated on the wall, far from one another.
verses.4:14: In whatever place you hear the sound of the ram's horn, gather to us there. Our God will fight for us."
verses.4:15: So we were doing the work, while half of them held the spears from the rising of the dawn until the stars came out.
verses.4:16: At that time I also said to the people, "Let each man and his attendant spend the night inside Jerusalem, so that they may be a guard for us by night and labor by day."
verses.4:17: So neither I, nor my brothers, nor my attendants, nor the men of the guard who followed me—none of us took off our clothes; each man kept his weapon even at the water.
verses.5:1: Now there was a great outcry from the people and their wives against their Jewish brothers.
verses.5:2: There were those who said, "We, with our sons and our daughters, are many; let us get grain so that we may eat and live."
verses.5:3: And there were those who said, "We are pledging our fields, our vineyards, and our houses so that we may get grain in the famine."
verses.5:4: And there were those who said, "We have borrowed silver for the king's tax on our fields and our vineyards.
verses.5:5: And now, our flesh is like the flesh of our brothers, our children are like their children; yet look, we are forcing our sons and our daughters to be slaves, and some of our daughters have been brought into bondage, and there is no power in our hand, since our fields and our vineyards belong to others."
verses.5:6: I became very angry when I heard their outcry and these words.
verses.5:7: I took counsel within myself, and I contended with the nobles and the officials and said to them, "You are exacting interest, each man from his brother!" So I held a great assembly against them.
verses.5:8: And I said to them, "As far as we were able, we have bought back our Jewish brothers who were sold to the nations; and now will you even sell your brothers, so that they must be sold to us?" Then they kept silent and could find no reply.
verses.5:9: So I said, "The thing that you are doing is not good. Should you not walk in the fear of our God because of the reproach of the nations, our enemies?
verses.5:10: Moreover, I, my brothers, and my attendants are lending them silver and grain. Please, let us give up this interest.
verses.5:11: Please, return to them this very day their fields, their vineyards, their olive groves, and their houses, along with the hundredth part of the silver, the grain, the new wine, and the fresh oil that you are exacting from them."
verses.5:12: Then they said, "We will return it and will demand nothing from them; we will do just as you say." So I summoned the priests and put them under oath to act according to this promise.
verses.5:13: I also shook out the fold of my garment and said, "In this way may God shake out every man who does not uphold this promise from his house and from his earnings, and in this way may he be shaken out and left empty." Then the entire assembly said, "Amen," and praised the LORD; and the people acted according to this promise.
verses.5:14: Moreover, from the day that I was appointed to be their governor in the land of Judah, from the twentieth year to the thirty-second year of King Artaxerxes—twelve years—neither I nor my brothers ate the food of the governor.
verses.5:15: But the former governors who were before me laid heavy burdens on the people and took from them food and wine, besides forty shekels of silver; even their attendants lorded it over the people. Yet I did not do so, because of the fear of God.
verses.5:16: I also persevered in the work on this wall, and we bought no field; and all my attendants were gathered there for the work.
verses.5:17: Moreover, the Jews and the officials, one hundred and fifty men, as well as those who came to us from the nations that were around us, were at my table.
verses.5:18: Now what was prepared for each day was one ox and six choice sheep; fowl were also prepared for me, and every ten days all kinds of wine in abundance. Yet for all this, I did not demand the food of the governor, because the service was heavy upon this people.
verses.5:19: Remember for me, my God, for good, all that I have done for this people.
verses.6:1: Now when it was reported to Sanballat, Tobiah, Geshem the Arab, and the rest of our enemies that I had built the wall and that no breach remained in it, even though up to that time I had not set up doors in the gates,
verses.6:2: Sanballat and Geshem sent word to me, saying, "Come, let us meet together at Chephirim in the plain of Ono." But they were planning to do me harm.
verses.6:3: So I sent messengers to them, saying, "It is a great work that I am doing, and I am not able to go down. Why should the work cease while I let go of it and go down to you?"
verses.6:4: They sent to me in this same way four times, and I answered them in the same way.
verses.6:5: Then Sanballat sent his attendant to me in this same way a fifth time, with an open letter in his hand.
verses.6:6: In it was written, "It is reported among the nations, and Gashmu says, that you and the Jews are planning to rebel; therefore you are building the wall. And you are to become their king, according to these reports.
verses.6:7: You have also appointed prophets to proclaim concerning you in Jerusalem, saying, 'There is a king in Judah!' Now it will be reported to the king according to these words. So now come, and let us take counsel together."
verses.6:8: Then I sent word to him, saying, "No such things as you are saying have happened, for you are inventing them out of your own mind."
verses.6:9: For all of them were trying to intimidate us, saying, "Their hands will grow slack from the work, and it will not be done." But now, strengthen my hands!
verses.6:10: Now I went to the house of Shemaiah son of Delaiah, son of Mehetabel, who was shut in; and he said, "Let us meet together in the house of God, inside the temple, and let us close the doors of the temple, for they are coming to kill you—at night they are coming to kill you."
verses.6:11: Yet I answered, "Would a man like me flee? And who like me would enter the temple and live? I will not enter."
verses.6:12: Then I perceived that indeed God had not sent him; rather, he spoke the prophecy against me because Tobiah and Sanballat had hired him.
verses.6:13: For this reason he was hired: that I might be afraid, do so, and sin, so that they might have an evil report in order to reproach me.
verses.6:14: Remember, my God, Tobiah and Sanballat according to these deeds of theirs, and also Noadiah the prophetess and the rest of the prophets who were trying to intimidate me.
verses.6:15: Thus the wall was finished on the twenty-fifth of Elul, in fifty-two days.
verses.6:16: Now when all our enemies heard of it, all the nations that were around us were afraid, and they fell very low in their own eyes; and they knew that this work had been done by our God.
verses.6:17: Also in those days, the nobles of Judah were sending many letters to Tobiah, and letters from Tobiah were coming to them.
verses.6:18: For many in Judah were bound by oath to him, because he was the son-in-law of Shecaniah son of Arah, and his son Jehohanan had married the daughter of Meshullam son of Berechiah.
verses.6:19: They were also speaking of his good deeds before me, and they were reporting my words to him. Tobiah sent letters to intimidate me.
verses.7:1: Now when the wall was built and I had set the doors in place, the gatekeepers, the singers, and the Levites were appointed.
verses.7:2: Then I gave charge over Jerusalem to my brother Hanani and to Hananiah, the commander of the citadel, because he was truly a man of faithfulness and feared God more than many.
verses.7:3: I said to them, "The gates of Jerusalem are not to be opened until the sun grows hot, and while they are still standing on duty, let them close the doors, and bar them. Also station guards from the residents of Jerusalem, each man at his guard post and each man opposite his own house."
verses.7:4: Now the city was spacious and large, yet the people inside it were few, and no houses had been built.
verses.7:5: Then my God put it into my heart, and I gathered the nobles, the officials, and the people to be registered by genealogy. And I found the scroll of the genealogy of those who had come up at first, and I found written in it:
verses.7:6: These are the people of the province who came up from the captivity of the exile, whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had exiled. They returned to Jerusalem and to Judah, each man to his own city.
verses.7:7: They were the ones who came with Zerubbabel, Jeshua, Nehemiah, Azariah, Raamiah, Nahamani, Mordecai, Bilshan, Mispereth, Bigvai, Nehum, and Baanah. The count of the men of the people of Israel:
verses.7:8: The sons of Parosh: two thousand one hundred seventy-two.
verses.7:9: The sons of Shephatiah: three hundred seventy-two.
verses.7:10: The sons of Arah: six hundred fifty-two.
verses.7:11: The sons of Pahath-moab, of the sons of Jeshua and Joab: two thousand eight hundred eighteen.
verses.7:12: The sons of Elam: one thousand two hundred fifty-four.
verses.7:13: The sons of Zattu: eight hundred forty-five.
verses.7:14: The sons of Zaccai: seven hundred sixty.
verses.7:15: The sons of Binnui: six hundred forty-eight.
verses.7:16: The sons of Bebai: six hundred twenty-eight.
verses.7:17: The sons of Azgad: two thousand three hundred twenty-two.
verses.7:18: The sons of Adonikam: six hundred sixty-seven.
verses.7:19: The sons of Bigvai: two thousand sixty-seven.
verses.7:20: The sons of Adin: six hundred fifty-five.
verses.7:21: The sons of Ater, of Hezekiah: ninety-eight.
verses.7:22: The sons of Hashum: three hundred twenty-eight.
verses.7:23: The sons of Bezai: three hundred twenty-four.
verses.7:24: The sons of Hariph: one hundred twelve.
verses.7:26: The men of Bethlehem and Netophah: one hundred eighty-eight.
verses.7:27: The men of Anathoth: one hundred twenty-eight.
verses.7:29: The men of Kiriath-jearim, Chephirah, and Beeroth: seven hundred forty-three.
verses.7:30: The men of Ramah and Geba: six hundred twenty-one.
verses.7:31: The men of Michmas: one hundred twenty-two.
verses.7:32: The men of Bethel and Ai: one hundred twenty-three.
verses.7:33: The men of the other Nebo: fifty-two.
verses.7:34: The sons of the other Elam: one thousand two hundred fifty-four.

verses.7:38: The sons of Senaah: three thousand nine hundred thirty.
verses.7:39: The priests: the sons of Jedaiah, of the house of Jeshua, nine hundred seventy-three.
verses.7:40: The sons of Immer: one thousand fifty-two.
verses.7:41: The sons of Pashhur: one thousand two hundred forty-seven.
verses.7:42: The sons of Harim: one thousand seventeen.
verses.7:43: The Levites: the sons of Jeshua, of Kadmiel, from the sons of Hodevah, seventy-four.
verses.7:44: The singers: the sons of Asaph, one hundred forty-eight.
verses.7:45: The gatekeepers: the sons of Shallum, the sons of Ater, the sons of Talmon, the sons of Akkub, the sons of Hatita, and the sons of Shobai, one hundred thirty-eight.
verses.7:46: The temple servants: the sons of Ziha, the sons of Hasupha, the sons of Tabbaoth,
verses.7:47: the sons of Keros, the sons of Sia, the sons of Padon,
verses.7:48: the sons of Lebanah, the sons of Hagaba, the sons of Shalmai,
verses.7:49: the sons of Hanan, the sons of Giddel, the sons of Gahar,
verses.7:50: the sons of Reaiah, the sons of Rezin, the sons of Nekoda,
verses.7:51: the sons of Gazzam, the sons of Uzza, the sons of Paseah,
verses.7:52: the sons of Besai, the sons of Meunim, the sons of Nephishesim,
verses.7:53: the sons of Bakbuk, the sons of Hakupha, the sons of Harhur,
verses.7:54: the sons of Bazlith, the sons of Mehida, the sons of Harsha,
verses.7:55: the sons of Barkos, the sons of Sisera, the sons of Temah,
verses.7:56: the sons of Neziah, and the sons of Hatipha.
verses.7:57: The sons of Solomon's servants: the sons of Sotai, the sons of Sophereth, the sons of Perida,
verses.7:58: the sons of Jaala, the sons of Darkon, the sons of Giddel,
verses.7:59: the sons of Shephatiah, the sons of Hattil, the sons of Pochereth-hazzebaim, and the sons of Amon.
verses.7:60: All the temple servants and the sons of Solomon's servants: three hundred ninety-two.
verses.7:61: And these are the ones who came up from Tel-melah, Tel-harsha, Cherub, Addon, and Immer, yet they were unable to declare their fathers' house or their seed, whether they were from Israel:
verses.7:62: The sons of Delaiah, the sons of Tobiah, and the sons of Nekoda: six hundred forty-two.
verses.7:63: And from the priests: the sons of Hobaiah, the sons of Hakkoz, and the sons of Barzillai, who had taken a wife from among the daughters of Barzillai the Gileadite and was called by their name.
verses.7:64: These searched for their record among those registered by genealogy, but it was not found, so they were disqualified as unclean from the priesthood.
verses.7:65: And the governor told them that they must not eat from the most holy things until the priest should arise with Urim and Thummim.
verses.7:66: The entire assembly together numbered forty-two thousand three hundred sixty,
verses.7:67: apart from their male servants and female servants, who numbered seven thousand three hundred thirty-seven; and they had two hundred forty-five male singers and female singers.
verses.7:69: Camels: four hundred thirty-five; donkeys: six thousand seven hundred twenty.
verses.7:70: And some of the heads of the fathers' houses gave for the work. The governor gave to the treasury one thousand drachmas of gold, fifty basins, and five hundred thirty priests' tunics.
verses.7:71: And some of the heads of the fathers' houses gave to the treasury of the work twenty thousand drachmas of gold and two thousand two hundred minas of silver.
verses.7:72: And what the remainder of the people gave was twenty thousand drachmas of gold, two thousand minas of silver, and sixty-seven priests' tunics.
verses.7:73: So the priests, the Levites, the gatekeepers, the singers, some of the people, the temple servants, and all Israel settled in their cities. And the seventh month arrived while the sons of Israel were in their cities.
verses.8:1: Then all the people assembled as one man into the plaza that was in front of the Water Gate, and they told Ezra the scribe to bring the book of the law of Moses, which the LORD had commanded Israel.
verses.8:2: So Ezra the priest brought the law before the assembly, both men and women and everyone able to hear with understanding, on the first day of the seventh month.
verses.8:3: He read from it facing the plaza that was in front of the Water Gate from first light until midday, in the presence of the men, the women, and those who could understand, and the ears of all the people were turned toward the book of the law.
verses.8:4: Ezra the scribe stood on a wooden platform that they had made for the occasion. Standing beside him on his right were Mattithiah, Shema, Anaiah, Uriah, Hilkiah, and Maaseiah, and on his left were Pedaiah, Mishael, Malchijah, Hashum, Hashbaddanah, Zechariah, and Meshullam.
verses.8:5: Then Ezra opened the book before the eyes of all the people, for he was above all the people; and as he opened it, all the people stood up.
verses.8:6: Ezra blessed the LORD, the great God, and all the people answered, "Amen, Amen," lifting up their hands. Then they bowed low and worshiped the LORD with their faces to the ground.
verses.8:7: Also Jeshua, Bani, Sherebiah, Jamin, Akkub, Shabbethai, Hodiah, Maaseiah, Kelita, Azariah, Jozabad, Hanan, Pelaiah, and the Levites were helping the people understand the law, while the people remained in their place.
verses.8:8: They read distinctly from the book, from the law of God, and gave the meaning, so that they understood what was read.
verses.8:9: Then Nehemiah, who was the governor, and Ezra the priest and scribe, and the Levites who were giving the people understanding said to all the people, "This day is holy to the LORD your God; do not mourn and do not weep." For all the people were weeping when they heard the words of the law.
verses.8:10: Then he said to them, "Go, eat rich foods and drink sweet drinks, and send portions to the one for whom nothing is prepared, for this day is holy to our Lord. And do not be sorrowful, for the joy of the LORD is your stronghold."
verses.8:11: And the Levites were quieting all the people, saying, "Be quiet, for this day is holy, and do not be sorrowful."
verses.8:12: Then all the people went away to eat and to drink, to send portions, and to celebrate with great joy, because they understood the words that had been made known to them.
verses.8:13: On the second day, the heads of the fathers' houses of all the people, the priests, and the Levites gathered to Ezra the scribe in order to gain insight into the words of the law.
verses.8:14: And they found written in the law, which the LORD had commanded by the hand of Moses, that the sons of Israel should live in booths during the feast in the seventh month,
verses.8:15: and that they should announce and send out a proclamation in all their cities and in Jerusalem, saying, "Go out to the hill country and bring branches of olive, branches of wild olive, branches of myrtle, branches of palms, and branches of leafy trees to make booths, as it is written."
verses.8:16: So the people went out and brought them and made booths for themselves, each on his roof, and in their courtyards, and in the courtyards of the house of God, and in the plaza of the Water Gate, and in the plaza of the Gate of Ephraim.
verses.8:17: The entire assembly of those who had returned from the captivity made booths and lived in the booths. For from the days of Joshua the son of Nun until that day, the sons of Israel had not done so, and there was very great joy.
verses.8:18: Day by day, from the first day until the last day, he read from the book of the law of God. They observed the feast for seven days, and on the eighth day there was a solemn assembly according to the ordinance.
verses.9:1: Now on the twenty-fourth day of this month, the sons of Israel assembled with fasting, in sackcloth, and with earth on them.
verses.9:2: The seed of Israel separated themselves from all foreigners, and they stood and confessed their sins and the iniquities of their fathers.
verses.9:3: They stood up in their place and read from the book of the law of the LORD their God for a fourth of the day, and for another fourth they were confessing and worshiping the LORD their God.
verses.9:4: Now on the steps of the Levites stood Jeshua, Bani, Kadmiel, Shebaniah, Bunni, Sherebiah, Bani, and Chenani, and they cried out with a loud voice to the LORD their God.
verses.9:5: Then the Levites Jeshua, Kadmiel, Bani, Hashabneiah, Sherebiah, Hodiah, Shebaniah, and Pethahiah said, "Rise and bless the LORD your God from everlasting to everlasting. Let them bless Your glorious name, which is exalted above all blessing and praise.
verses.9:6: You alone are the LORD; You made the heavens, the heaven of heavens and all their host, the earth and everything on it, the seas and everything in them. You keep all of them alive, and the host of heaven worships You.
verses.9:7: You are the LORD God, who chose Abram, brought him out of Ur of the Chaldeans, and gave him the name Abraham.
verses.9:8: You found his heart faithful before You, and You made the covenant with him to give the land of the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Amorites, the Perizzites, the Jebusites, and the Girgashites—to give it to his seed. And You have fulfilled Your words, for You are righteous.
verses.9:9: You saw the affliction of our fathers in Egypt, and You heard their outcry at the Sea of Reeds.
verses.9:10: You performed signs and wonders against Pharaoh, against all his servants, and against all the people of his land, because You knew that they had acted arrogantly against them; and You made a name for Yourself, as it is this day.
verses.9:11: You split the sea before them, and they crossed through the middle of the sea on dry ground; their pursuers You threw into the depths, like a stone into mighty waters.
verses.9:12: With a pillar of cloud You led them by day, and with a pillar of fire by night, to light up for them the way in which they were to go.
verses.9:13: You came down upon Mount Sinai and spoke with them from heaven, and You gave them upright ordinances and laws of truth, good statutes and commandments.
verses.9:14: You made known to them Your holy Sabbath, and commandments, statutes, and law You commanded for them by the hand of Moses Your servant.
verses.9:15: You gave them bread from heaven for their hunger, and You brought out water for them from a rock for their thirst; and You told them to go in to possess the land that You had lifted up Your hand to give to them.
verses.9:16: Yet they and our fathers acted arrogantly; they stiffened their neck and did not listen to Your commandments.
verses.9:17: They refused to listen and did not remember Your wondrous deeds that You had done with them; instead, they stiffened their neck and appointed a leader to return to their slavery in their rebellion. Yet You are a God of forgiveness, gracious and compassionate, slow to anger and abounding in loyal love, and You did not abandon them.
verses.9:18: Even when they made for themselves a calf of cast metal and said, 'This is your god who brought you up out of Egypt,' and committed great blasphemies,
verses.9:19: You, in Your great compassion, did not abandon them in the wilderness. The pillar of cloud did not depart from over them by day to lead them along the way, nor did the pillar of fire by night to give light to them and to the way in which they were to go.
verses.9:20: You gave Your good Spirit to impart insight to them; You did not withhold Your manna from their mouths, and You gave them water for their thirst.
verses.9:21: For forty years You sustained them in the wilderness, so that they were not in want; their garments did not wear out, and their feet did not swell.
verses.9:22: You gave them kingdoms and peoples and apportioned them to every boundary. So they took possession of the land of Sihon, even the land of the king of Heshbon, and the land of Og king of Bashan.
verses.9:23: You multiplied their sons like the stars of heaven, and You brought them into the land that You had told their fathers to go in to possess.
verses.9:24: So the sons went in and took possession of the land, and You subdued before them the inhabitants of the land, the Canaanites, and gave them into their hand—both their kings and the peoples of the land—to do with them according to their will.
verses.9:25: They captured fortified cities and rich soil, and took possession of houses filled with all good things, hewn cisterns, vineyards, olive groves, and fruit trees in abundance. So they ate, were satisfied, grew fat, and delighted themselves in Your great goodness.
verses.9:26: But they grew defiant and rebelled against You; they cast Your law behind their backs and killed Your prophets, who had warned them to turn them back to You, and they committed great blasphemies.
verses.9:27: Therefore You gave them into the hand of their oppressors, who oppressed them. But in the time of their distress they cried out to You, and You heard from heaven; and according to Your great compassion You gave them deliverers who delivered them from the hand of their oppressors.
verses.9:28: Yet as soon as they had rest, they again did evil before You, so You abandoned them into the hand of their enemies, who ruled over them. Then they cried out to You again, and You heard from heaven and rescued them according to Your compassion many times.
verses.9:29: You warned them in order to turn them back to Your law, yet they acted arrogantly and did not listen to Your commandments, but sinned against Your ordinances—which, if anyone does them, he will live by them—and they turned a stubborn shoulder, stiffened their neck, and would not listen.
verses.9:30: For many years You bore with them and warned them by Your Spirit through the hand of Your prophets, yet they would not give ear. Therefore You gave them into the hand of the peoples of the lands.
verses.9:31: Yet in Your great compassion You did not make a complete end of them or abandon them, for You are a gracious and compassionate God.
verses.9:32: Now therefore, our God—the great, mighty, and awesome God, who keeps the covenant and loyal love—do not let all the hardship seem small before You that has come upon us, upon our kings, upon our officials, upon our priests, upon our prophets, upon our fathers, and upon all Your people, from the days of the kings of Assyria until this day.
verses.9:33: Yet You are righteous concerning all that has come upon us, for You have acted in truth, while we have acted wickedly.
verses.9:34: Our kings, our officials, our priests, and our fathers did not practice Your law, nor did they pay attention to Your commandments or to Your testimonies with which You warned them.
verses.9:35: Even in their kingdom, amid Your abundant goodness that You gave them, and in the broad and rich land that You set before them, they did not serve You, nor did they turn from their evil deeds.
verses.9:36: Look, we are slaves today; and as for the land that You gave to our fathers to eat its fruit and its bounty, look, we are slaves on it.
verses.9:37: And its produce abounds for the kings whom You have set over us because of our sins; they rule over our bodies and over our livestock according to their will, and we are in great distress."
verses.10:1: And because of all this, we are making a binding agreement and writing it down, and on the sealed document are our officials, our Levites, and our priests.
verses.10:2: And on the sealed documents were Nehemiah the governor, the son of Hacaliah, and Zedekiah.
verses.10:9: Maaziah, Bilgai, and Shemaiah. These were the priests.
verses.10:10: And the Levites: Jeshua the son of Azaniah, Binnui of the sons of Henadad, Kadmiel,
verses.10:11: and their brothers: Shebaniah, Hodiah, Kelita, Pelaiah, Hanan,
verses.10:15: The heads of the people: Parosh, Pahath-moab, Elam, Zattu, Bani,
verses.10:29: And the rest of the people—the priests, the Levites, the gatekeepers, the singers, the temple servants, and all who separated themselves from the peoples of the lands to the law of God, their wives, their sons, and their daughters, everyone with knowledge and discernment—
verses.10:30: join firmly with their brothers, their nobles, and enter into a curse and an oath to walk in the law of God, which was given by the hand of Moses the servant of God, and to keep and perform all the commandments of the LORD our Lord, and His judgments and His statutes;
verses.10:31: and that we will not give our daughters to the peoples of the land, nor will we take their daughters for our sons.
verses.10:32: And as for the peoples of the land who bring merchandise or any grain to sell on the Sabbath day, we will not buy from them on the Sabbath or on a holy day; and we will forgo the seventh year and the debt-claim of every hand.
verses.10:33: We have also established obligations on ourselves to levy a third of a shekel on ourselves each year for the service of the house of our God:
verses.10:34: for the bread set in rows, the continual grain offering, and the continual burnt offering, for the Sabbaths, the new moons, and the appointed festivals, for the sacred things, and for the sin offerings to make atonement for Israel, and all the work of the house of our God.
verses.10:35: We also cast lots—the priests, the Levites, and the people—regarding the wood offering, to bring it to the house of our God by our fathers' houses at designated times, year by year, to burn upon the altar of the LORD our God, as is written in the law;
verses.10:36: and to bring the firstfruits of our soil and the firstfruits of all fruit of every tree, year by year, to the house of the LORD;
verses.10:37: and to bring the firstborn of our sons and of our livestock, as is written in the law, and the firstborn of our herds and our flocks, to the house of our God, to the priests who minister in the house of our God.
verses.10:38: And we will bring the first of our dough, our contributions, the fruit of every tree, new wine, and fresh oil to the priests, to the chambers of the house of our God, and the tithe of our soil to the Levites; for the Levites themselves are the ones who collect the tithes in all the cities of our labor.
verses.10:39: And the priest, the son of Aaron, will be with the Levites when the Levites collect the tithes, and the Levites will bring up the tithe of the tithe to the house of our God, to the chambers, to the storehouse.
verses.10:40: For the sons of Israel and the sons of Levi will bring the contribution of the grain, the new wine, and the fresh oil to the chambers; and there are the vessels of the sanctuary, and the priests who minister, and the gatekeepers, and the singers. And we will not forsake the house of our God.
verses.11:1: Now the officials of the people lived in Jerusalem, and the rest of the people cast lots to bring one out of ten to live in Jerusalem, the holy city, while the nine parts lived in the cities.
verses.11:2: And the people blessed all the men who offered themselves freely to live in Jerusalem.
verses.11:3: Now these are the heads of the province who lived in Jerusalem; but in the cities of Judah they lived, each man in his possession in their cities: Israel, the priests, the Levites, the temple servants, and the sons of Solomon's servants.
verses.11:4: And in Jerusalem lived some of the sons of Judah and some of the sons of Benjamin. Of the sons of Judah: Athaiah the son of Uzziah, the son of Zechariah, the son of Amariah, the son of Shephatiah, the son of Mahalalel, from the sons of Perez;
verses.11:5: and Maaseiah the son of Baruch, the son of Col-hozeh, the son of Hazaiah, the son of Adaiah, the son of Joiarib, the son of Zechariah, the son of the Shilonite.
verses.11:6: All the sons of Perez who lived in Jerusalem were four hundred sixty-eight men of valor.
verses.11:7: And these are the sons of Benjamin: Sallu the son of Meshullam, the son of Joed, the son of Pedaiah, the son of Kolaiah, the son of Maaseiah, the son of Ithiel, the son of Jeshaiah.
verses.11:8: And after him were Gabbai and Sallai, nine hundred twenty-eight.
verses.11:9: And Joel the son of Zichri was overseer over them, and Judah the son of Hassenuah was second in rank over the city.
verses.11:10: Of the priests: Jedaiah the son of Joiarib, Jachin,
verses.11:11: Seraiah the son of Hilkiah, the son of Meshullam, the son of Zadok, the son of Meraioth, the son of Ahitub, ruler of the house of God;
verses.11:12: and their brothers who carried out the work for the house, eight hundred twenty-two; and Adaiah the son of Jeroham, the son of Pelaliah, the son of Amzi, the son of Zechariah, the son of Pashhur, the son of Malchijah,
verses.11:13: and his brothers, heads of fathers' houses, two hundred forty-two; and Amashsai the son of Azarel, the son of Ahzai, the son of Meshillemoth, the son of Immer,
verses.11:14: and their brothers, mighty men of valor, one hundred twenty-eight. And Zabdiel the son of Haggedolim was overseer over them.
verses.11:15: And of the Levites: Shemaiah the son of Hasshub, the son of Azrikam, the son of Hashabiah, the son of Bunni;
verses.11:17: and Mattaniah the son of Mica, the son of Zabdi, the son of Asaph, who was the leader to start giving thanks in prayer, and Bakbukiah, the second in rank among his brothers, and Abda the son of Shammua, the son of Galal, the son of Jeduthun.
verses.11:18: All the Levites in the holy city were two hundred eighty-four.
verses.11:19: And the gatekeepers—Akkub, Talmon, and their brothers who kept guard at the gates—were one hundred seventy-two.
verses.11:22: And the overseer of the Levites in Jerusalem was Uzzi the son of Bani, the son of Hashabiah, the son of Mattaniah, the son of Mica, from the sons of Asaph, the singers, in charge of the work of the house of God.
verses.11:23: For the command of the king was concerning them, and there was a binding provision regarding the singers, as each day required.
verses.11:24: And Pethahiah the son of Meshezabel, from the sons of Zerah the son of Judah, was at the king's hand in every matter for the people.
verses.11:25: And regarding the villages in their fields, some of the sons of Judah lived in Kiriath-arba and its dependent towns, and in Dibon and its dependent towns, and in Jekabzeel and its villages,
verses.11:26: and in Jeshua, and in Moladah, and in Beth-pelet,
verses.11:27: and in Hazar-shual, and in Beersheba and its dependent towns,
verses.11:30: Zanoah, Adullam, and their villages, Lachish and its fields, Azekah and its dependent towns. And they encamped from Beersheba to the Valley of Hinnom.
verses.11:31: And the sons of Benjamin lived starting from Geba, in Michmash and Aija, and in Bethel and its dependent towns.
verses.11:36: And from the Levites, divisions of Judah were attached to Benjamin.
verses.12:1: And these are the priests and the Levites who went up with Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, and Jeshua: Seraiah, Jeremiah, Ezra,
verses.12:7: Sallu, Amok, Hilkiah, Jedaiah: these were the heads of the priests and of their brothers in the days of Jeshua.
verses.12:8: And the Levites were Jeshua, Binnui, Kadmiel, Sherebiah, Judah, and Mattaniah; he and his brothers were over the songs of thanksgiving.
verses.12:9: And Bakbukiah and Unni, their brothers, were opposite them for the watches.
verses.12:10: And Jeshua fathered Joiakim, and Joiakim fathered Eliashib, and Eliashib fathered Joiada.
verses.12:11: And Joiada fathered Jonathan, and Jonathan fathered Jaddua.
verses.12:12: And in the days of Joiakim, there were priests, heads of the fathers' houses: for Seraiah, Meraiah; for Jeremiah, Hananiah;
verses.12:13: for Ezra, Meshullam; for Amariah, Jehohanan;
verses.12:14: for Melichu, Jonathan; for Shebaniah, Joseph;
verses.12:15: for Harim, Adna; for Meraioth, Helkai;
verses.12:16: for Iddo, Zechariah; for Ginnethon, Meshullam;
verses.12:17: for Abijah, Zichri; for Miniamin; for Moadiah, Piltai;
verses.12:18: for Bilgah, Shammua; for Shemaiah, Jehonathan;
verses.12:19: and for Joiarib, Mattenai; for Jedaiah, Uzzi;
verses.12:20: for Sallai, Kallai; for Amok, Eber;
verses.12:21: for Hilkiah, Hashabiah; for Jedaiah, Nethanel.
verses.12:22: The Levites in the days of Eliashib, Joiada, Johanan, and Jaddua were recorded as heads of fathers' houses, and the priests as well, during the reign of Darius the Persian.
verses.12:23: The sons of Levi, the heads of the fathers' houses, were recorded in the book of the chronicles, even until the days of Johanan son of Eliashib.
verses.12:24: And the heads of the Levites were Hashabiah, Sherebiah, and Jeshua son of Kadmiel, with their brothers opposite them, to praise and to give thanks, by the command of David the man of God, watch corresponding to watch.
verses.12:25: Mattaniah and Bakbukiah, Obadiah, Meshullam, Talmon, and Akkub were gatekeepers who kept watch at the storehouses of the gates.
verses.12:26: These were in the days of Joiakim son of Jeshua, son of Jozadak, and in the days of Nehemiah the governor and Ezra the priest, the scribe.
verses.12:27: And at the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem, they searched for the Levites from all their places to bring them to Jerusalem, to observe the dedication with joy, with thanksgivings and with song, with cymbals, harps, and lyres.
verses.12:28: And the sons of the singers assembled, both from the region around Jerusalem and from the villages of the Netophathites,
verses.12:29: and from Beth-gilgal and from the fields of Geba and Azmaveth, because the singers had built villages for themselves around Jerusalem.
verses.12:30: Then the priests and the Levites purified themselves, and they purified the people, the gates, and the wall.
verses.12:31: Then I brought the leaders of Judah up onto the wall, and I stationed two large thanksgiving choirs and processions. One went to the right atop the wall toward the Dung Gate.
verses.12:32: And Hoshaiah and half of the leaders of Judah walked behind them,
verses.12:34: Judah and Benjamin, and Shemaiah and Jeremiah,
verses.12:35: and some from the sons of the priests with trumpets: Zechariah son of Jonathan, son of Shemaiah, son of Mattaniah, son of Micaiah, son of Zaccur, son of Asaph,
verses.12:36: and his brothers, Shemaiah, Azarel, Milalai, Gilalai, Maai, Nethanel, Judah, and Hanani, with the musical instruments of David the man of God; and Ezra the scribe was in front of them.
verses.12:37: And at the Fountain Gate, straight ahead of them, they went up the steps of the city of David by the ascent to the wall, above the house of David, and as far as the Water Gate on the east.
verses.12:38: And the second thanksgiving choir went in the opposite direction, and I was behind it with half of the people atop the wall, above the Tower of the Ovens and as far as the Broad Wall,
verses.12:39: and above the Gate of Ephraim, and by the Old Gate, and by the Fish Gate, the Tower of Hananel, and the Tower of the Hundred, as far as the Sheep Gate; and they stood still at the Gate of the Guard.
verses.12:40: Then the two thanksgiving choirs stood in the house of God, and I also, with half of the officials with me,
verses.12:41: and the priests—Eliakim, Maaseiah, Miniamin, Micaiah, Elioenai, Zechariah, and Hananiah—with trumpets,
verses.12:42: and Maaseiah, Shemaiah, Eleazar, Uzzi, Jehohanan, Malchijah, Elam, and Ezer. And the singers made their voices heard, with Jezrahiah as the overseer.
verses.12:43: And they offered great sacrifices on that day and rejoiced, because God had caused them to rejoice with great joy; and the women and the children rejoiced as well, so that the joy of Jerusalem was heard from far away.
verses.12:44: And on that day men were appointed over the chambers for the stores, the contributions, the firstfruits, and the tithes, to collect into them, from the fields of the cities, the portions prescribed by the law for the priests and for the Levites; for Judah took joy in the priests and in the Levites who stood in service.
verses.12:45: And they kept the charge of their God and the charge of purification, along with the singers and the gatekeepers, according to the command of David and his son Solomon.
verses.12:46: For in the days of David and Asaph long ago, there were heads of the singers, and songs of praise and thanksgivings to God.
verses.12:47: And all Israel in the days of Zerubbabel and in the days of Nehemiah gave the portions of the singers and the gatekeepers, each day's requirement in its day; and they consecrated the portions for the Levites, and the Levites consecrated the portions for the sons of Aaron.
verses.13:1: On that day the book of Moses was read in the people's hearing, and it was found written in it that no Ammonite or Moabite may ever enter the assembly of God,
verses.13:2: because they did not come out to meet the sons of Israel with bread and water; rather, they hired Balaam against them to curse them, yet our God changed the curse into a blessing.
verses.13:3: Now when they heard the law, they separated everyone of mixed descent from Israel.
verses.13:4: Prior to this, Eliashib the priest, having been placed in charge of the chamber of the house of our God, was a relative of Tobiah,
verses.13:5: and he prepared a large chamber for him, where previously they used to place the grain offering, the frankincense, the vessels, and the tithe of the grain, the new wine, and the fresh oil—the prescribed portion for the Levites, the singers, and the gatekeepers—and the contribution for the priests.
verses.13:6: During all this I was not in Jerusalem, for in the thirty-second year of Artaxerxes king of Babylon I had gone to the king; then after some days I requested leave from the king.
verses.13:7: So I came to Jerusalem, and I perceived the evil that Eliashib had done for Tobiah in preparing a chamber for him in the courtyards of the house of God.
verses.13:8: It displeased me greatly, and I threw all the household furnishings of Tobiah out of the chamber.
verses.13:9: Then I gave a command, and they purified the chambers; and I returned there the vessels of the house of God, the grain offering, and the frankincense.
verses.13:10: I also learned that the Levites' portions had not been given, so the Levites and the singers doing the work had fled, each man to his field.
verses.13:11: So I contended with the officials and said, "Why has the house of God been abandoned?" Then I gathered them and stationed them at their post.
verses.13:12: Then all of Judah brought the tithe of the grain, the new wine, and the fresh oil to the storehouses.
verses.13:13: And I appointed as treasurers over the storehouses Shelemiah the priest, Zadok the scribe, and Pedaiah of the Levites, and as their aide, Hanan son of Zaccur, son of Mattaniah; for they were regarded as trustworthy, and the responsibility of distributing to their brothers rested upon them.
verses.13:14: Remember me for this, my God, and do not erase my acts of loyal love that I have done for the house of my God and for its services.
verses.13:15: In those days I saw in Judah some who were treading winepresses on the Sabbath, bringing in heaps of grain and loading them on donkeys, as well as wine, grapes, figs, and every kind of load, and bringing them into Jerusalem on the Sabbath day. So I solemnly warned them on the day they sold provisions.
verses.13:16: And Tyrians lived there, bringing in fish and all sorts of wares, and selling them on the Sabbath to the sons of Judah, and in Jerusalem.
verses.13:17: Then I contended with the nobles of Judah and said to them, "What is this evil thing you are doing, desecrating the Sabbath day?
verses.13:18: Did your fathers not do like this, so that our God brought all this evil on us and on this city? Yet you are adding fierce wrath against Israel by desecrating the Sabbath."
verses.13:19: When the gates of Jerusalem fell into shadow before the Sabbath, I gave a command and the doors were shut, and I ordered that they not open them until after the Sabbath. And I stationed some of my attendants at the gates so that no load would enter on the Sabbath day.
verses.13:20: So the traders and the sellers of every kind of merchandise spent the night outside Jerusalem once or twice.
verses.13:21: Then I solemnly warned them and said to them, "Why are you spending the night in front of the wall? If you do this a second time, I will lay a hand on you." From that time forward they did not come on the Sabbath.
verses.13:22: Then I instructed the Levites that they should purify themselves and come to guard the gates in order to sanctify the Sabbath day. Remember me for this also, my God, and spare me according to the abundance of Your loyal love.
verses.13:23: Also in those days I saw the Jews who had married Ashdodite, Ammonite, and Moabite women.
verses.13:24: Of their children, half spoke the language of Ashdod, and they did not know how to speak the language of Judah, but spoke according to the language of each people.
verses.13:25: So I contended with them, cursed them, beat some of the men among them, and pulled out their hair; and I put them under oath by God: "You are not to give your daughters to their sons, nor take any of their daughters for your sons or for yourselves.
verses.13:26: Did Solomon king of Israel not sin because of these things? Among the many nations there was not a king like him; he was loved by his God, and God appointed him king over all Israel. Still, the foreign women caused even him to sin.
verses.13:27: And should we listen to you and commit all this great evil, breaking faith with our God by marrying foreign women?"
verses.13:28: Now one of the sons of Joiada, son of Eliashib the high priest, was a son-in-law to Sanballat the Horonite, and I drove him away from my presence.
verses.13:29: Remember them, my God, on account of the defiling of the priesthood and of the covenant of the priesthood and the Levites.
verses.13:30: So I purified them from all that was foreign, and I set up duties for the priests and for the Levites, each man in his work,
verses.13:31: and for the wood offering at designated times, and for the firstfruits. Remember me for good, my God.

notes.1:8: Hebrew omits an explicit conjunction for 'if' here and at the beginning of 1:9, expressing the conditional clauses through juxtaposed statements.
notes.1:9: Ketiv writes an irregular form (whbw'tym), whereas Qere reads the regular Hiphil waw-consecutive perfect of bw' (wahabi'otim, 'and I will bring them').
notes.2:8: 'the temple' is literally 'the house' (Hebrew habbayit), referring here to the temple in distinction from Nehemiah's own residence ('the house that I will enter') at the end of the clause.
notes.2:10: 'servant' (Hebrew ebed) likely serves here as a Persian administrative title ('official') for Tobiah in Ammon, while preserving the literal term contrasted with 'His servants' in 2:20.
notes.2:13: Ketiv writes hmprwṣym as one word with a medial mem, whereas Qere divides it into two words, hem perusim ('which were broken down').
notes.2:20: 'right' renders Hebrew sedaqa ('righteousness'), used here in its legal sense of a valid claim or standing.
notes.3:5: 'their lords' translates plural Hebrew adonehem, which may refer to the supervisors directing the work or, as a plural of majesty, to 'their Lord' (God) or the governor.
notes.3:8: 'restored' renders Hebrew azab II ('repair, fortify'), distinct from azab I ('leave, forsake'); the same verb recurs in 3:34, where some instead read azab I ('Will they be left to themselves?').
notes.3:15: Ketiv reads plural wy'mydw ('and they set up'), whereas Qere reads singular weya'amid ('and set up'), matching the singular subject Shallun.
notes.3:20: Ketiv reads zby (Zabbai), whereas Qere reads zakkay (Zaccai). 'zealously repaired' translates the rare asyndetic pairing of Hiphil hehera ('burned with zeal') and Hiphil heheziq ('repaired').
notes.3:30: In both 3:30 and 3:31, Ketiv reads 'hry ('after me'), whereas Qere reads aharaw ('after him'), matching the third-person sequence of the list.
notes.3:37: 'provoked anger' renders Hiphil hik'isu used without an explicit object, an idiom denoting that they provoked God to anger in the sight of the builders.
notes.4:6: The Hebrew clause beginning with 'from all the places' (mikkol-hammeqomot asher-tashuvu alenu) is notoriously terse. Here asher is taken as introducing speech (as elsewhere in Nehemiah) and al as 'to,' rendering a plea from the outlying Jews for the builders to return home, though others construe it elliptically as a warning of attacks from every direction.
notes.4:7: Translates the Qere batsehihim ('in the exposed places'); the Ketiv btshhyym transposes the medial yod and chet. Hebrew repeats the verb "I stationed" (wa'a'amid) before naming the object "the people" (et-ha'am).
notes.4:9: Translates the Qere wannashov ('and we returned,' standard Qal wayyiqtol 1cp of shuv); the Ketiv wnshwb reflects a fuller spelling of the verb.
notes.4:17: The final three Hebrew words (ish shilho hammayim, literally 'each man his weapon, the water') are famously elliptical, generally understood to mean that each man kept his weapon with him even when going to the water.
notes.5:7: Translates the Qere noshim (Qal active participle of nashah, 'exacting interest' or 'a loan-claim'); the Ketiv nsh'ym reflects the interchange of nashah with nasha or nasa ('imposing'). The opening verb wayyimmalekh (Niphal of malakh, influenced by Aramaic melakh, 'counsel') literally means 'my heart took counsel within me.'
notes.5:9: Translates the Qere wa'omar ('and I said,' first-person singular matching Nehemiah's memoir); the Ketiv reads third-person wy'mr ('and he said').
notes.5:11: Hebrew ume'at literally means 'and the hundredth part,' widely understood as a monthly one-percent interest rate (twelve percent annually) charged on loans of silver and produce.
notes.5:15: The terse phrase belehem wayayin ahar kesef-sheqalim arba'im uses ahar ('after') in the sense of 'besides' or 'in addition to' forty shekels of silver.
notes.6:2: Hebrew bakkephirim is vocalized as a plural proper place name ('at Chephirim,' compare Chephirah in Neh 7:29), though many interpreters take it as a variant plural of kaphar meaning 'in the villages.'
notes.6:9: The Piel imperative hazzeq ('strengthen') is an abrupt prayer addressed to God without an explicit vocative in the Hebrew text.
notes.6:14: Hebrew kema'asaw elleh literally reads 'according to these deeds of his,' with the third-person masculine singular suffix agreeing with the first-named subject, Tobiah, while encompassing both men.
notes.6:16: Hebrew wayyir'u, written with a single yod and a meteg under the hireq, is translated here as a defective Qal wayyiqtol of yare' ('were afraid,' reversing the intimidation motif of 6:9, 13-14, 19); it can also be read as the Qal of ra'ah ('saw [it]').
notes.7:2: The prefixed preposition on "man of faithfulness" functions as a kaph of confirmation ("truly a man of faithfulness"); the pronoun "he" is singular, referring specifically to Hananiah.
notes.7:3: The written text (ketiv) reads "and he said," while the read tradition (qere) followed here reads "and I said." The verb translated "close" is a Hiphil form occurring only here in Biblical Hebrew, and "station" renders a Hiphil infinitive absolute functioning as an imperative.
notes.7:4: The word translated "spacious" is literally "wide of hands," a Hebrew idiom meaning broad and expansive in every direction.
notes.7:33: Hebrew distinguishes "the other Nebo" here and "the other Elam" in 7:34 from identically named places or clans; the register also alternates between "sons of" (7:8-25, 34-38) and "men of" (7:26-33).
notes.7:52: The written text (ketiv) spells the name "Nephushesim," while the read tradition (qere) followed here reads "Nephishesim."
notes.7:64: The verb translated "disqualified as unclean" is a Pual form of a root meaning to defile or declare ritually impure, distinct from the homonymous root meaning to redeem.
notes.7:65: The title translated "governor" is the Persian loanword tirshatha, used for the Persian-appointed ruler of Judah.
notes.7:69: Verse 68, which lists horses and mules in some later manuscripts and ancient versions (compare Ezra 2:66), is absent from the Masoretic Text here.
notes.7:70: The Hebrew term darkemonim refers to gold coins (drachmas or Persian darics). The Masoretic Text literally gives the count of priests' tunics as "30 and 500" (530).
notes.8:6: The noun translated "lifting up" (Hebrew mo'al) is a hapax legomenon derived from the root 'alah ("go up"), referring to raising the hands in prayer and blessing.
notes.8:8: The Pual participle mephorash ("distinctly") can also mean "with translation" or "paragraph by paragraph" (cf. the cognate Aramaic participle in Ezra 4:18). The verb wayyavinu with bammiqra' is taken intransitively as "they understood what was read" (cf. v. 12), though it could also be parsed as a causative Hiphil meaning "they gave understanding of the reading."
notes.8:9: The title "the governor" renders the Persian loanword hattirshata', used of the governor of Judah (cf. Ezra 2:63; Neh 7:65, 70; 10:2).
notes.8:10: The noun ma'oz ("stronghold") denotes a fortified refuge or place of strength.
notes.9:5: In the Masoretic Text, the Levites' call to worship shifts directly to second-person prayer to God in the second half of this verse and continues through v. 37 without naming a new speaker (unlike the Septuagint, which inserts Ezra before v. 6).
notes.9:6: Ketiv reads 't (a rare defective spelling of the second-person masculine singular pronoun); Qere reads 'attah ("You"), which is followed here.
notes.9:17: Ketiv reads wchsd (with an extra conjunction waw); Qere reads chesed, forming werav-chesed ("and abounding in loyal love"), which is followed here. In addition, the Masoretic Text reads bemiryam ("in their rebellion"), whereas some ancient versions harmonize to "in Egypt."
notes.9:22: The clause "apportioned them to every boundary" (literally "apportioned them to a corner/border") idiomatically refers to dividing and allotting territories to every district. The Masoretic Text then repeats "the land" epexegetically ("the land of Sihon, even the land of the king of Heshbon").
notes.9:32: The particle 'et here introduces the grammatical subject ("all the hardship"), a syntactic usage attested in Late Biblical Hebrew (similarly in vv. 19 and 34).
notes.10:2: The phrase on the sealed documents translates the masculine plural Qal passive participle hachatumim, paralleling the singular hechatum in 10:1 and indicating either the sealed documents or those who set their seals. Governor translates hattirshata, a Persian administrative title.
notes.10:20: Translates the qere Nebai; the ketiv reads Nobai.
notes.10:30: Join firmly translates the Hiphil participle machaziqim with the preposition al, literally holding fast upon, expressing firm solidarity in taking the covenant oath.
notes.10:32: The Hebrew literally reads we will leave off the seventh year and the exaction of every hand, referring to letting the land lie fallow in the sabbatical year and canceling every creditor's claim.
notes.10:39: When the Levites collect the tithes translates the syncopated Hiphil infinitive construct baaser, matching the Piel participle measserim in 10:38; both stems here denote collecting the tithes.
notes.11:14: Haggedolim is a Hebrew plural form meaning the great ones, here treated as a family or ancestral name; it may alternatively be rendered the son of the great men.
notes.11:17: Translates the qere Jeduthun; the ketiv reads Jedithun. The phrase leader to start giving thanks in prayer renders the Masoretic Hebrew rosh hattechillah yehodeh lattephillah, literally head of the beginning, he gives thanks for the prayer, with the Hiphil imperfect yehodeh retaining its he.
notes.11:24: At the king's hand translates the Hebrew idiom leyad hammelek, denoting service as the king's advisor or liaison.
notes.11:25: Dependent towns here and in 11:27, 30, and 31 translates Hebrew banot, literally daughters, denoting satellite towns attached to a mother city, in distinction from chatserim, unwalled villages.
notes.11:36: The Hebrew is a terse verbless clause literally reading And from the Levites, divisions of Judah for Benjamin, indicating that certain Levitical divisions from Judah were assigned to Benjamin's territory.
notes.12:14: The translation follows the Qere (read form) Melichu; the Ketiv (written form) reads Malluchi (compare Malluch in 12:2).
notes.12:16: The translation follows the Qere (read form) Iddo; the Ketiv (written form) reads Adaiah (or Iddia).
notes.12:17: In the Masoretic Text, no personal name follows for Miniamin; the phrase carries a disjunctive accent directly before for Moadiah, Piltai, indicating an apparent omission in the Hebrew text.
notes.12:31: Hebrew todot literally means thanksgivings, here denoting choirs giving thanks, and tahalukot is a rare noun meaning processions found only here. The words One went are implied by the contrast with the second thanksgiving choir in 12:38.
notes.12:46: The translation follows the Qere (read form), plural construct heads of the singers; the Ketiv (written form) reads singular head of the singers.
notes.13:13: The verb wa'otserah is a rare denominative Hiphil of 'atsar (from 'otsar, storehouse/treasury), meaning appointed as treasurers, forming a wordplay with 'otsarot (storehouses).
notes.13:19: The Qal verb tsalelu (from tsalal, related to tsel, shadow) occurs only here in the Hebrew Bible in the sense of growing dark or falling into shadow, with the gates of Jerusalem as its grammatical subject.
notes.13:23: Ketiv writes the plene forms for Ashdodite and Ammonite while Qere reads the defective forms with no difference in meaning. The Hiphil verb hoshivu (from yashav, literally caused to dwell) is a Late Biblical Hebrew idiom used here and in 13:27 for marrying foreign women.
notes.13:25: Literally "if you give... and if you take," a standard Hebrew elliptical oath formula after the Hiphil verb of swearing (wa'ashbi'em) expressing an emphatic negative prohibition.
notes.13:27: The form hanishma' can be parsed as Qal imperfect 1cp ("should we listen" or "do we hear") or identically vocalized Niphal perfect 3ms ("has it been heard"), yielding either "should we listen to you" or "must we hear concerning you."
