native_verses.1:1: The words of Nehemiah son of Hacaliah. It came about in the month of Kislev, in the twentieth year, when I was in Susa the citadel,
native_verses.1:2: that Hanani, one of my brothers, arrived—he and men from Judah—and I asked them about the Jews, the escaped remnant who were left from the captivity, and about Jerusalem.
native_verses.1:3: They said to me, "The remnant who are left from the captivity there in the province are in great distress and in reproach, and the wall of Jerusalem is broken down, and its gates have been burned with fire."
native_verses.1:4: When I heard these words, I sat down and wept, and I mourned for days; and I continued fasting and praying before the God of heaven.
native_verses.1:5: And I said, "Please, LORD, God of heaven, the great and awesome God, who keeps the covenant and loyal love for those who love Him and keep His commandments:
native_verses.1:6: let Your ear please be attentive and Your eyes open to listen to the prayer of Your servant, which I am praying before You today, day and night, on behalf of the sons of Israel, Your servants, while confessing the sins of the sons of Israel that we have sinned against You. Both I and my father's house have sinned.
native_verses.1:7: We have indeed acted corruptly against You, and we have not kept the commandments, the statutes, and the ordinances that You commanded Your servant Moses.
native_verses.1:8: Please remember the word that You commanded Your servant Moses, saying, 'If you act unfaithfully, I will scatter you among the peoples;
native_verses.1:9: but if you return to Me and keep My commandments and do them, even if your outcasts are at the end of the heavens, from there I will gather them and bring them to the place that I have chosen to make My name dwell there.'
native_verses.1:10: Now they are Your servants and Your people, whom You redeemed by Your great power and by Your strong hand.
native_verses.1:11: Please, Lord, let Your ear be attentive to the prayer of Your servant and to the prayer of Your servants who take delight in fearing Your name; and please grant success to Your servant today, and grant him compassion before this man." Now I was cupbearer to the king.
native_verses.2:1: It came about in the month of Nisan, in the twentieth year of King Artaxerxes, when wine was before him, that I took up the wine and gave it to the king. Now I had not been sad in his presence.
native_verses.2:2: So the king said to me, "Why is your face sad, though you are not sick? This is nothing other than sadness of heart." Then I was very much afraid.
native_verses.2:3: I said to the king, "May the king live forever! Why should my face not be sad, when the city, the place of my fathers' tombs, lies desolate, and its gates have been consumed by fire?"
native_verses.2:4: Then the king said to me, "What is it that you are requesting?" So I prayed to the God of heaven.
native_verses.2:5: And I said to the king, "If it seems good to the king, and if your servant is pleasing before you, send me to Judah, to the city of my fathers' tombs, that I may rebuild it."
native_verses.2:6: Then the king said to me—with the queen sitting beside him—"How long will your journey be, and when will you return?" So it pleased the king to send me, and I gave him a set time.
native_verses.2:7: And I said to the king, "If it seems good to the king, let letters be given to me for the governors of Beyond the River, that they may let me pass through until I arrive in Judah,
native_verses.2:8: and a letter to Asaph, the keeper of the king's forest, that he may give me timber to lay beams for the gates of the citadel belonging to the temple, and for the wall of the city, and for the house that I will enter." And the king granted them to me, according to the good hand of my God upon me.
native_verses.2:9: Then I came to the governors of Beyond the River and gave them the king's letters. Now the king had sent army officers and horsemen with me.
native_verses.2:10: When Sanballat the Horonite and Tobiah the Ammonite servant heard of it, it was greatly displeasing to them that a man had come to seek the good of the sons of Israel.
native_verses.2:11: So I came to Jerusalem and was there three days.
native_verses.2:12: Then I arose in the night, I and a few men with me; and I did not tell anyone what my God was putting into my heart to do for Jerusalem. And there was no animal with me except the animal on which I was riding.
native_verses.2:13: So I went out by the Valley Gate at night, toward the front of the Dragon Spring and to the Dung Gate; and I was inspecting the walls of Jerusalem, which were broken down, and its gates had been consumed by fire.
native_verses.2:14: Then I passed on to the Fountain Gate and to the King's Pool, but there was no room for the animal under me to pass.
native_verses.2:15: So I went up along the valley at night and continued inspecting the wall; then I turned back, entered through the Valley Gate, and returned.
native_verses.2:16: And the officials did not know where I had gone or what I was doing, nor had I yet told the Jews, the priests, the nobles, the officials, or the rest of those doing the work.
native_verses.2:17: Then I said to them, "You see the distress we are in, how Jerusalem lies desolate and its gates are burned with fire. Come, let us rebuild the wall of Jerusalem, so that we may no longer be a reproach."
native_verses.2:18: And I told them about the hand of my God, which had been good upon me, and also the king's words that he had spoken to me. And they said, "Let us arise and build." So they strengthened their hands for the good cause.
native_verses.2:19: But when Sanballat the Horonite, Tobiah the Ammonite servant, and Geshem the Arab heard of it, they mocked us and despised us, and said, "What is this thing that you are doing? Are you rebelling against the king?"
native_verses.2:20: So I gave them an answer and said to them, "The God of heaven—He will grant us success, and we, His servants, will arise and build; but as for you, you have no portion, right, or memorial in Jerusalem."
native_verses.3:1: Then Eliashib the high priest arose with his brothers the priests, and they built the Sheep Gate. They consecrated it and set up its doors; they consecrated it as far as the Tower of the Hundred, as far as the Tower of Hananel.
native_verses.3:2: And next to him the men of Jericho built. And next to him Zaccur son of Imri built.
native_verses.3:3: Now the sons of Hassenaah built the Fish Gate; they laid its beams and set up its doors, its bolts, and its bars.
native_verses.3:4: Next to them Meremoth son of Uriah, son of Hakkoz, made repairs. Next to them Meshullam son of Berechiah, son of Meshezabel, made repairs. Next to them Zadok son of Baana made repairs.
native_verses.3:5: Next to them the Tekoites made repairs, but their nobles did not put their necks to the work of their lords.
native_verses.3:6: Joiada son of Paseah and Meshullam son of Besodeiah repaired the Old Gate; they laid its beams and set up its doors, its bolts, and its bars.
native_verses.3:7: And next to them, Melatiah the Gibeonite and Jadon the Meronothite, the men of Gibeon and Mizpah belonging to the seat of the governor of Beyond the River, made repairs.
native_verses.3:8: Next to him Uzziel son of Harhaiah, of the goldsmiths, made repairs. And next to him Hananiah, one of the perfumers, made repairs; and they restored Jerusalem as far as the Broad Wall.
native_verses.3:9: Next to them Rephaiah son of Hur, ruler of half the district of Jerusalem, made repairs.
native_verses.3:10: Next to them Jedaiah son of Harumaph made repairs, even opposite his house. And next to him Hattush son of Hashabneiah made repairs.
native_verses.3:11: Malchijah son of Harim and Hasshub son of Pahath-moab repaired another section and the Tower of the Ovens.
native_verses.3:12: Next to him Shallum son of Hallohesh, ruler of half the district of Jerusalem, made repairs—he and his daughters.
native_verses.3:13: Hanun and the inhabitants of Zanoah repaired the Valley Gate; they built it and set up its doors, its bolts, and its bars, along with a thousand cubits of the wall as far as the Dung Gate.
native_verses.3:14: Malchijah son of Rechab, ruler of the district of Beth-haccherem, repaired the Dung Gate; he built it and set up its doors, its bolts, and its bars.
native_verses.3:15: Shallun son of Col-hozeh, ruler of the district of Mizpah, repaired the Fountain Gate; he built it, roofed it, and set up its doors, its bolts, and its bars. He also repaired the wall of the Pool of Shelah by the king's garden, as far as the stairs that go down from the City of David.
native_verses.3:16: After him Nehemiah son of Azbuk, ruler of half the district of Beth-zur, made repairs to a point opposite the tombs of David, and as far as the constructed pool, and as far as the House of the Mighty Men.
native_verses.3:17: After him the Levites made repairs: Rehum son of Bani. Next to him Hashabiah, ruler of half the district of Keilah, made repairs for his district.
native_verses.3:18: After him their brothers made repairs: Bavvai son of Henadad, ruler of half the district of Keilah.
native_verses.3:19: Next to him Ezer son of Jeshua, ruler of Mizpah, repaired another section opposite the ascent to the armory at the Angle.
native_verses.3:20: After him Baruch son of Zaccai zealously repaired another section, from the Angle to the doorway of the house of Eliashib the high priest.
native_verses.3:21: After him Meremoth son of Uriah, son of Hakkoz, repaired another section, from the doorway of the house of Eliashib to the end of the house of Eliashib.
native_verses.3:22: After him the priests, the men of the plain, made repairs.
native_verses.3:23: After him Benjamin and Hasshub made repairs opposite their house. After him Azariah son of Maaseiah, son of Ananiah, made repairs beside his house.
native_verses.3:24: After him Binnui son of Henadad repaired another section, from the house of Azariah to the Angle and to the Corner.
native_verses.3:25: Palal son of Uzai made repairs opposite the Angle and the tower projecting from the upper house of the king, which is by the court of the guard. After him Pedaiah son of Parosh made repairs.
native_verses.3:26: Now the temple servants were dwelling on Ophel, as far as a point opposite the Water Gate on the east and the projecting tower.
native_verses.3:27: After him the Tekoites repaired another section, from opposite the great projecting tower to the wall of Ophel.
native_verses.3:28: Above the Horse Gate the priests made repairs, each one opposite his house.
native_verses.3:29: After him Zadok son of Immer made repairs opposite his house. And after him Shemaiah son of Shecaniah, the keeper of the East Gate, made repairs.
native_verses.3:30: After him Hananiah son of Shelemiah and Hanun, the sixth son of Zalaph, repaired another section. After him Meshullam son of Berechiah made repairs opposite his chamber.
native_verses.3:31: After him Malchijah, one of the goldsmiths, made repairs as far as the house of the temple servants and of the merchants, opposite the Inspection Gate, and as far as the upper chamber of the Corner.
native_verses.3:32: And between the upper chamber of the Corner and the Sheep Gate, the goldsmiths and the merchants made repairs.
native_verses.3:33: Now when Sanballat heard that we were building the wall, he burned with anger and was greatly indignant, and he mocked the Jews.
native_verses.3:34: And he spoke before his brothers and the army of Samaria, and said, "What are the feeble Jews doing? Will they restore it for themselves? Will they offer sacrifices? Will they finish in a day? Will they revive the stones from the heaps of dust, burned as they are?"
native_verses.3:35: Now Tobiah the Ammonite was beside him, and he said, "Even what they are building—if a fox goes up on it, it will break down their stone wall!"
native_verses.3:36: Hear, our God, for we have become an object of contempt; turn back their reproach upon their own head, and give them over as plunder in a land of captivity.
native_verses.3:37: Do not cover their iniquity, and do not let their sin be blotted out from before You, for they have provoked anger in front of the builders.
native_verses.3:38: So we built the wall, and the entire wall was connected up to half its height, for the people had a heart to work.
native_verses.4:1: Now when Sanballat, Tobiah, the Arabs, the Ammonites, and the Ashdodites heard that repair was going forward on the walls of Jerusalem, that the breaches had begun to be closed up, they became very angry.
native_verses.4:2: All of them conspired together to come and fight against Jerusalem and to cause confusion in it.
native_verses.4:3: Yet we prayed to our God, and we stationed a guard against them day and night on account of them.
native_verses.4:4: Then Judah said, "The strength of the burden-bearer has faltered, and there is much rubble, and we are not able to build on the wall."
native_verses.4:5: And our adversaries said, "They will not know and will not see until we come into their midst and kill them and make the work cease."
native_verses.4:6: Now when the Jews who lived beside them came, they told us ten times from all the places, "You must return to us."
native_verses.4:7: So I stationed the people in the lowest parts of the space behind the wall, in the exposed places—I stationed them by families, with their swords, their spears, and their bows.
native_verses.4:8: Then I looked, and I rose and said to the nobles, to the officials, and to the rest of the people, "Do not fear them! Remember the great and awesome Lord, and fight for your brothers, your sons and your daughters, your wives and your houses."
native_verses.4:9: Now when our enemies heard that it was known to us and that God had thwarted their plan, all of us returned to the wall, each man to his work.
native_verses.4:10: From that day on, half of my attendants were doing the work while half of them held the spears, the shields, the bows, and the coats of mail, and the leaders were behind the entire house of Judah.
native_verses.4:11: Those who were building on the wall and those who were carrying burdens were loading up: with one hand each was doing the work, and the other held a weapon.
native_verses.4:12: And as for the builders, each man had his sword strapped to his waist as they built; and the one who blew the ram's horn was beside me.
native_verses.4:13: And I said to the nobles, to the officials, and to the rest of the people, "The work is great and extensive, and we are separated on the wall, far from one another.
native_verses.4:14: In whatever place you hear the sound of the ram's horn, gather to us there. Our God will fight for us."
native_verses.4:15: So we were doing the work, while half of them held the spears from the rising of the dawn until the stars came out.
native_verses.4:16: At that time I also said to the people, "Let each man and his attendant spend the night inside Jerusalem, so that they may be a guard for us by night and labor by day."
native_verses.4:17: So neither I, nor my brothers, nor my attendants, nor the men of the guard who followed me—none of us took off our clothes; each man kept his weapon even at the water.
native_verses.5:1: Now there was a great outcry from the people and their wives against their Jewish brothers.
native_verses.5:2: There were those who said, "We, with our sons and our daughters, are many; let us get grain so that we may eat and live."
native_verses.5:3: And there were those who said, "We are pledging our fields, our vineyards, and our houses so that we may get grain in the famine."
native_verses.5:4: And there were those who said, "We have borrowed silver for the king's tax on our fields and our vineyards.
native_verses.5:5: And now, our flesh is like the flesh of our brothers, our children are like their children; yet look, we are forcing our sons and our daughters to be slaves, and some of our daughters have been brought into bondage, and there is no power in our hand, since our fields and our vineyards belong to others."
native_verses.5:6: I became very angry when I heard their outcry and these words.
native_verses.5:7: I took counsel within myself, and I contended with the nobles and the officials and said to them, "You are exacting interest, each man from his brother!" So I held a great assembly against them.
native_verses.5:8: And I said to them, "As far as we were able, we have bought back our Jewish brothers who were sold to the nations; and now will you even sell your brothers, so that they must be sold to us?" Then they kept silent and could find no reply.
native_verses.5:9: So I said, "The thing that you are doing is not good. Should you not walk in the fear of our God because of the reproach of the nations, our enemies?
native_verses.5:10: Moreover, I, my brothers, and my attendants are lending them silver and grain. Please, let us give up this interest.
native_verses.5:11: Please, return to them this very day their fields, their vineyards, their olive groves, and their houses, along with the hundredth part of the silver, the grain, the new wine, and the fresh oil that you are exacting from them."
native_verses.5:12: Then they said, "We will return it and will demand nothing from them; we will do just as you say." So I summoned the priests and put them under oath to act according to this promise.
native_verses.5:13: I also shook out the fold of my garment and said, "In this way may God shake out every man who does not uphold this promise from his house and from his earnings, and in this way may he be shaken out and left empty." Then the entire assembly said, "Amen," and praised the LORD; and the people acted according to this promise.
native_verses.5:14: Moreover, from the day that I was appointed to be their governor in the land of Judah, from the twentieth year to the thirty-second year of King Artaxerxes—twelve years—neither I nor my brothers ate the food of the governor.
native_verses.5:15: But the former governors who were before me laid heavy burdens on the people and took from them food and wine, besides forty shekels of silver; even their attendants lorded it over the people. Yet I did not do so, because of the fear of God.
native_verses.5:16: I also persevered in the work on this wall, and we bought no field; and all my attendants were gathered there for the work.
native_verses.5:17: Moreover, the Jews and the officials, one hundred and fifty men, as well as those who came to us from the nations that were around us, were at my table.
native_verses.5:18: Now what was prepared for each day was one ox and six choice sheep; fowl were also prepared for me, and every ten days all kinds of wine in abundance. Yet for all this, I did not demand the food of the governor, because the service was heavy upon this people.
native_verses.5:19: Remember for me, my God, for good, all that I have done for this people.
native_verses.6:1: Now when it was reported to Sanballat, Tobiah, Geshem the Arab, and the rest of our enemies that I had built the wall and that no breach remained in it, even though up to that time I had not set up doors in the gates,
native_verses.6:2: Sanballat and Geshem sent word to me, saying, "Come, let us meet together at Chephirim in the plain of Ono." But they were planning to do me harm.
native_verses.6:3: So I sent messengers to them, saying, "It is a great work that I am doing, and I am not able to go down. Why should the work cease while I let go of it and go down to you?"
native_verses.6:4: They sent to me in this same way four times, and I answered them in the same way.
native_verses.6:5: Then Sanballat sent his attendant to me in this same way a fifth time, with an open letter in his hand.
native_verses.6:6: In it was written, "It is reported among the nations, and Gashmu says, that you and the Jews are planning to rebel; therefore you are building the wall. And you are to become their king, according to these reports.
native_verses.6:7: You have also appointed prophets to proclaim concerning you in Jerusalem, saying, 'There is a king in Judah!' Now it will be reported to the king according to these words. So now come, and let us take counsel together."
native_verses.6:8: Then I sent word to him, saying, "No such things as you are saying have happened, for you are inventing them out of your own mind."
native_verses.6:9: For all of them were trying to intimidate us, saying, "Their hands will grow slack from the work, and it will not be done." But now, strengthen my hands!
native_verses.6:10: Now I went to the house of Shemaiah son of Delaiah, son of Mehetabel, who was shut in; and he said, "Let us meet together in the house of God, inside the temple, and let us close the doors of the temple, for they are coming to kill you—at night they are coming to kill you."
native_verses.6:11: Yet I answered, "Would a man like me flee? And who like me would enter the temple and live? I will not enter."
native_verses.6:12: Then I perceived that indeed God had not sent him; rather, he spoke the prophecy against me because Tobiah and Sanballat had hired him.
native_verses.6:13: For this reason he was hired: that I might be afraid, do so, and sin, so that they might have an evil report in order to reproach me.
native_verses.6:14: Remember, my God, Tobiah and Sanballat according to these deeds of theirs, and also Noadiah the prophetess and the rest of the prophets who were trying to intimidate me.
native_verses.6:15: Thus the wall was finished on the twenty-fifth of Elul, in fifty-two days.
native_verses.6:16: Now when all our enemies heard of it, all the nations that were around us were afraid, and they fell very low in their own eyes; and they knew that this work had been done by our God.
native_verses.6:17: Also in those days, the nobles of Judah were sending many letters to Tobiah, and letters from Tobiah were coming to them.
native_verses.6:18: For many in Judah were bound by oath to him, because he was the son-in-law of Shecaniah son of Arah, and his son Jehohanan had married the daughter of Meshullam son of Berechiah.
native_verses.6:19: They were also speaking of his good deeds before me, and they were reporting my words to him. Tobiah sent letters to intimidate me.
native_verses.7:1: Now when the wall was built and I had set the doors in place, the gatekeepers, the singers, and the Levites were appointed.
native_verses.7:2: Then I gave charge over Jerusalem to my brother Hanani and to Hananiah, the commander of the citadel, because he was truly a man of faithfulness and feared God more than many.
native_verses.7:3: I said to them, "The gates of Jerusalem are not to be opened until the sun grows hot, and while they are still standing on duty, let them close the doors, and bar them. Also station guards from the residents of Jerusalem, each man at his guard post and each man opposite his own house."
native_verses.7:4: Now the city was spacious and large, yet the people inside it were few, and no houses had been built.

native_verses.7:64: These searched for their record among those registered by genealogy, but it was not found, so they were disqualified as unclean from the priesthood.

native_verses.7:71: And what the remainder of the people gave was twenty thousand drachmas of gold, two thousand minas of silver, and sixty-seven priests' tunics.
native_verses.7:72: So the priests, the Levites, the gatekeepers, the singers, some of the people, the temple servants, and all Israel settled in their cities. And the seventh month arrived while the sons of Israel were in their cities.
native_verses.8:1: Then all the people assembled as one man into the plaza that was in front of the Water Gate, and they told Ezra the scribe to bring the book of the law of Moses, which the LORD had commanded Israel.
native_verses.8:2: So Ezra the priest brought the law before the assembly, both men and women and everyone able to hear with understanding, on the first day of the seventh month.
native_verses.8:3: He read from it facing the plaza that was in front of the Water Gate from first light until midday, in the presence of the men, the women, and those who could understand, and the ears of all the people were turned toward the book of the law.
native_verses.8:4: Ezra the scribe stood on a wooden platform that they had made for the occasion. Standing beside him on his right were Mattithiah, Shema, Anaiah, Uriah, Hilkiah, and Maaseiah, and on his left were Pedaiah, Mishael, Malchijah, Hashum, Hashbaddanah, Zechariah, and Meshullam.
native_verses.8:5: Then Ezra opened the book before the eyes of all the people, for he was above all the people; and as he opened it, all the people stood up.
native_verses.8:6: Ezra blessed the LORD, the great God, and all the people answered, "Amen, Amen," lifting up their hands. Then they bowed low and worshiped the LORD with their faces to the ground.
native_verses.8:7: Also Jeshua, Bani, Sherebiah, Jamin, Akkub, Shabbethai, Hodiah, Maaseiah, Kelita, Azariah, Jozabad, Hanan, Pelaiah, and the Levites were helping the people understand the law, while the people remained in their place.
native_verses.8:8: They read distinctly from the book, from the law of God, and gave the meaning, so that they understood what was read.
native_verses.8:9: Then Nehemiah, who was the governor, and Ezra the priest and scribe, and the Levites who were giving the people understanding said to all the people, "This day is holy to the LORD your God; do not mourn and do not weep." For all the people were weeping when they heard the words of the law.
native_verses.8:10: Then he said to them, "Go, eat rich foods and drink sweet drinks, and send portions to the one for whom nothing is prepared, for this day is holy to our Lord. And do not be sorrowful, for the joy of the LORD is your stronghold."
native_verses.8:11: And the Levites were quieting all the people, saying, "Be quiet, for this day is holy, and do not be sorrowful."
native_verses.8:12: Then all the people went away to eat and to drink, to send portions, and to celebrate with great joy, because they understood the words that had been made known to them.
native_verses.8:13: On the second day, the heads of the fathers' houses of all the people, the priests, and the Levites gathered to Ezra the scribe in order to gain insight into the words of the law.
native_verses.8:14: And they found written in the law, which the LORD had commanded by the hand of Moses, that the sons of Israel should live in booths during the feast in the seventh month,
native_verses.8:15: and that they should announce and send out a proclamation in all their cities and in Jerusalem, saying, "Go out to the hill country and bring branches of olive, branches of wild olive, branches of myrtle, branches of palms, and branches of leafy trees to make booths, as it is written."
native_verses.8:16: So the people went out and brought them and made booths for themselves, each on his roof, and in their courtyards, and in the courtyards of the house of God, and in the plaza of the Water Gate, and in the plaza of the Gate of Ephraim.
native_verses.8:17: The entire assembly of those who had returned from the captivity made booths and lived in the booths. For from the days of Joshua the son of Nun until that day, the sons of Israel had not done so, and there was very great joy.
native_verses.8:18: Day by day, from the first day until the last day, he read from the book of the law of God. They observed the feast for seven days, and on the eighth day there was a solemn assembly according to the ordinance.
native_verses.9:1: Now on the twenty-fourth day of this month, the sons of Israel assembled with fasting, in sackcloth, and with earth on them.
native_verses.9:2: The seed of Israel separated themselves from all foreigners, and they stood and confessed their sins and the iniquities of their fathers.
native_verses.9:3: They stood up in their place and read from the book of the law of the LORD their God for a fourth of the day, and for another fourth they were confessing and worshiping the LORD their God.
native_verses.9:4: Now on the steps of the Levites stood Jeshua, Bani, Kadmiel, Shebaniah, Bunni, Sherebiah, Bani, and Chenani, and they cried out with a loud voice to the LORD their God.
native_verses.9:5: Then the Levites Jeshua, Kadmiel, Bani, Hashabneiah, Sherebiah, Hodiah, Shebaniah, and Pethahiah said, "Rise and bless the LORD your God from everlasting to everlasting. Let them bless Your glorious name, which is exalted above all blessing and praise.
native_verses.9:6: You alone are the LORD; You made the heavens, the heaven of heavens and all their host, the earth and everything on it, the seas and everything in them. You keep all of them alive, and the host of heaven worships You.
native_verses.9:7: You are the LORD God, who chose Abram, brought him out of Ur of the Chaldeans, and gave him the name Abraham.
native_verses.9:8: You found his heart faithful before You, and You made the covenant with him to give the land of the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Amorites, the Perizzites, the Jebusites, and the Girgashites—to give it to his seed. And You have fulfilled Your words, for You are righteous.
native_verses.9:9: You saw the affliction of our fathers in Egypt, and You heard their outcry at the Sea of Reeds.
native_verses.9:10: You performed signs and wonders against Pharaoh, against all his servants, and against all the people of his land, because You knew that they had acted arrogantly against them; and You made a name for Yourself, as it is this day.
native_verses.9:11: You split the sea before them, and they crossed through the middle of the sea on dry ground; their pursuers You threw into the depths, like a stone into mighty waters.
native_verses.9:12: With a pillar of cloud You led them by day, and with a pillar of fire by night, to light up for them the way in which they were to go.
native_verses.9:13: You came down upon Mount Sinai and spoke with them from heaven, and You gave them upright ordinances and laws of truth, good statutes and commandments.
native_verses.9:14: You made known to them Your holy Sabbath, and commandments, statutes, and law You commanded for them by the hand of Moses Your servant.
native_verses.9:15: You gave them bread from heaven for their hunger, and You brought out water for them from a rock for their thirst; and You told them to go in to possess the land that You had lifted up Your hand to give to them.
native_verses.9:16: Yet they and our fathers acted arrogantly; they stiffened their neck and did not listen to Your commandments.
native_verses.9:17: They refused to listen and did not remember Your wondrous deeds that You had done with them; instead, they stiffened their neck and appointed a leader to return to their slavery in their rebellion. Yet You are a God of forgiveness, gracious and compassionate, slow to anger and abounding in loyal love, and You did not abandon them.
native_verses.9:18: Even when they made for themselves a calf of cast metal and said, 'This is your god who brought you up out of Egypt,' and committed great blasphemies,
native_verses.9:19: You, in Your great compassion, did not abandon them in the wilderness. The pillar of cloud did not depart from over them by day to lead them along the way, nor did the pillar of fire by night to give light to them and to the way in which they were to go.
native_verses.9:20: You gave Your good Spirit to impart insight to them; You did not withhold Your manna from their mouths, and You gave them water for their thirst.
native_verses.9:21: For forty years You sustained them in the wilderness, so that they were not in want; their garments did not wear out, and their feet did not swell.
native_verses.9:22: You gave them kingdoms and peoples and apportioned them to every boundary. So they took possession of the land of Sihon, even the land of the king of Heshbon, and the land of Og king of Bashan.
native_verses.9:23: You multiplied their sons like the stars of heaven, and You brought them into the land that You had told their fathers to go in to possess.
native_verses.9:24: So the sons went in and took possession of the land, and You subdued before them the inhabitants of the land, the Canaanites, and gave them into their hand—both their kings and the peoples of the land—to do with them according to their will.
native_verses.9:25: They captured fortified cities and rich soil, and took possession of houses filled with all good things, hewn cisterns, vineyards, olive groves, and fruit trees in abundance. So they ate, were satisfied, grew fat, and delighted themselves in Your great goodness.
native_verses.9:26: But they grew defiant and rebelled against You; they cast Your law behind their backs and killed Your prophets, who had warned them to turn them back to You, and they committed great blasphemies.
native_verses.9:27: Therefore You gave them into the hand of their oppressors, who oppressed them. But in the time of their distress they cried out to You, and You heard from heaven; and according to Your great compassion You gave them deliverers who delivered them from the hand of their oppressors.
native_verses.9:28: Yet as soon as they had rest, they again did evil before You, so You abandoned them into the hand of their enemies, who ruled over them. Then they cried out to You again, and You heard from heaven and rescued them according to Your compassion many times.
native_verses.9:29: You warned them in order to turn them back to Your law, yet they acted arrogantly and did not listen to Your commandments, but sinned against Your ordinances—which, if anyone does them, he will live by them—and they turned a stubborn shoulder, stiffened their neck, and would not listen.
native_verses.9:30: For many years You bore with them and warned them by Your Spirit through the hand of Your prophets, yet they would not give ear. Therefore You gave them into the hand of the peoples of the lands.
native_verses.9:31: Yet in Your great compassion You did not make a complete end of them or abandon them, for You are a gracious and compassionate God.
native_verses.9:32: Now therefore, our God—the great, mighty, and awesome God, who keeps the covenant and loyal love—do not let all the hardship seem small before You that has come upon us, upon our kings, upon our officials, upon our priests, upon our prophets, upon our fathers, and upon all Your people, from the days of the kings of Assyria until this day.
native_verses.9:33: Yet You are righteous concerning all that has come upon us, for You have acted in truth, while we have acted wickedly.
native_verses.9:34: Our kings, our officials, our priests, and our fathers did not practice Your law, nor did they pay attention to Your commandments or to Your testimonies with which You warned them.
native_verses.9:35: Even in their kingdom, amid Your abundant goodness that You gave them, and in the broad and rich land that You set before them, they did not serve You, nor did they turn from their evil deeds.
native_verses.9:36: Look, we are slaves today; and as for the land that You gave to our fathers to eat its fruit and its bounty, look, we are slaves on it.
native_verses.9:37: And its produce abounds for the kings whom You have set over us because of our sins; they rule over our bodies and over our livestock according to their will, and we are in great distress."

native_verses.10:29: And the rest of the people—the priests, the Levites, the gatekeepers, the singers, the temple servants, and all who separated themselves from the peoples of the lands to the law of God, their wives, their sons, and their daughters, everyone with knowledge and discernment—

native_verses.10:38: And we will bring the first of our dough, our contributions, the fruit of every tree, new wine, and fresh oil to the priests, to the chambers of the house of our God, and the tithe of our soil to the Levites; for the Levites themselves are the ones who collect the tithes in all the cities of our labor.

native_notes.1:8: Hebrew omits an explicit conjunction for 'if' here and at the beginning of 1:9, expressing the conditional clauses through juxtaposed statements.
native_notes.1:9: Ketiv writes an irregular form (whbw'tym), whereas Qere reads the regular Hiphil waw-consecutive perfect of bw' (wahabi'otim, 'and I will bring them').
native_notes.2:8: 'the temple' is literally 'the house' (Hebrew habbayit), referring here to the temple in distinction from Nehemiah's own residence ('the house that I will enter') at the end of the clause.
native_notes.2:10: 'servant' (Hebrew ebed) likely serves here as a Persian administrative title ('official') for Tobiah in Ammon, while preserving the literal term contrasted with 'His servants' in 2:20.
native_notes.2:13: Ketiv writes hmprwṣym as one word with a medial mem, whereas Qere divides it into two words, hem perusim ('which were broken down').
native_notes.2:20: 'right' renders Hebrew sedaqa ('righteousness'), used here in its legal sense of a valid claim or standing.
native_notes.3:5: 'their lords' translates plural Hebrew adonehem, which may refer to the supervisors directing the work or, as a plural of majesty, to 'their Lord' (God) or the governor.
native_notes.3:7: The Hebrew phrase translated "belonging to the seat" may indicate that Gibeon and Mizpah were under the administrative jurisdiction of the Persian governor of Trans-Euphrates, or that they repaired up to his official residence.
native_notes.3:8: 'restored' renders Hebrew azab II ('repair, fortify'), distinct from azab I ('leave, forsake'); the same verb recurs in 3:34, where some instead read azab I ('Will they be left to themselves?').
native_notes.3:15: Ketiv reads plural wy'mydw ('and they set up'), whereas Qere reads singular weya'amid ('and set up'), matching the singular subject Shallun.
native_notes.3:20: Ketiv reads zby (Zabbai), whereas Qere reads zakkay (Zaccai). 'zealously repaired' translates the rare asyndetic pairing of Hiphil hehera ('burned with zeal') and Hiphil heheziq ('repaired').
native_notes.3:30: In both 3:30 and 3:31, Ketiv reads 'hry ('after me'), whereas Qere reads aharaw ('after him'), matching the third-person sequence of the list.
native_notes.3:37: 'provoked anger' renders Hiphil hik'isu used without an explicit object, an idiom denoting that they provoked God to anger in the sight of the builders.
native_notes.4:6: The Hebrew clause beginning with 'from all the places' (mikkol-hammeqomot asher-tashuvu alenu) is notoriously terse. Here asher is taken as introducing speech (as elsewhere in Nehemiah) and al as 'to,' rendering a plea from the outlying Jews for the builders to return home, though others construe it elliptically as a warning of attacks from every direction.
native_notes.4:7: Translates the Qere batsehihim ('in the exposed places'); the Ketiv btshhyym transposes the medial yod and chet. Hebrew repeats the verb "I stationed" (wa'a'amid) before naming the object "the people" (et-ha'am).
native_notes.4:9: Translates the Qere wannashov ('and we returned,' standard Qal wayyiqtol 1cp of shuv); the Ketiv wnshwb reflects a fuller spelling of the verb.
native_notes.4:17: The final three Hebrew words (ish shilho hammayim, literally 'each man his weapon, the water') are famously elliptical, generally understood to mean that each man kept his weapon with him even when going to the water.
native_notes.5:7: Translates the Qere noshim (Qal active participle of nashah, 'exacting interest' or 'a loan-claim'); the Ketiv nsh'ym reflects the interchange of nashah with nasha or nasa ('imposing'). The opening verb wayyimmalekh (Niphal of malakh, influenced by Aramaic melakh, 'counsel') literally means 'my heart took counsel within me.'
native_notes.5:9: Translates the Qere wa'omar ('and I said,' first-person singular matching Nehemiah's memoir); the Ketiv reads third-person wy'mr ('and he said').
native_notes.5:11: Hebrew ume'at literally means 'and the hundredth part,' widely understood as a monthly one-percent interest rate (twelve percent annually) charged on loans of silver and produce.
native_notes.5:15: The terse phrase belehem wayayin ahar kesef-sheqalim arba'im uses ahar ('after') in the sense of 'besides' or 'in addition to' forty shekels of silver.
native_notes.6:2: Hebrew bakkephirim is vocalized as a plural proper place name ('at Chephirim,' compare Chephirah in Neh 7:29), though many interpreters take it as a variant plural of kaphar meaning 'in the villages.'
native_notes.6:9: The Piel imperative hazzeq ('strengthen') is an abrupt prayer addressed to God without an explicit vocative in the Hebrew text.
native_notes.6:14: Hebrew kema'asaw elleh literally reads 'according to these deeds of his,' with the third-person masculine singular suffix agreeing with the first-named subject, Tobiah, while encompassing both men.
native_notes.6:16: Hebrew wayyir'u, written with a single yod and a meteg under the hireq, is translated here as a defective Qal wayyiqtol of yare' ('were afraid,' reversing the intimidation motif of 6:9, 13-14, 19); it can also be read as the Qal of ra'ah ('saw [it]').
native_notes.7:2: The prefixed preposition on "man of faithfulness" functions as a kaph of confirmation ("truly a man of faithfulness"); the pronoun "he" is singular, referring specifically to Hananiah.
native_notes.7:3: The written text (ketiv) reads "and he said," while the read tradition (qere) followed here reads "and I said." The verb translated "close" is a Hiphil form occurring only here in Biblical Hebrew, and "station" renders a Hiphil infinitive absolute functioning as an imperative.
native_notes.7:4: The word translated "spacious" is literally "wide of hands," a Hebrew idiom meaning broad and expansive in every direction.
native_notes.7:33: Hebrew distinguishes "the other Nebo" here and "the other Elam" in 7:34 from identically named places or clans; the register also alternates between "sons of" (7:8-25, 34-38) and "men of" (7:26-33).
native_notes.7:52: The written text (ketiv) spells the name "Nephushesim," while the read tradition (qere) followed here reads "Nephishesim."
native_notes.7:64: The verb translated "disqualified as unclean" is a Pual form of a root meaning to defile or declare ritually impure, distinct from the homonymous root meaning to redeem.
native_notes.7:65: The title translated "governor" is the Persian loanword tirshatha, used for the Persian-appointed ruler of Judah.
native_notes.7:68: Verse 68, which lists horses and mules in some later manuscripts and ancient versions (compare Ezra 2:66), is absent from the Masoretic Text here.
native_notes.7:69: The Hebrew term darkemonim refers to gold coins (drachmas or Persian darics). The Masoretic Text literally gives the count of priests' tunics as "30 and 500" (530).
native_notes.8:6: The noun translated "lifting up" (Hebrew mo'al) is a hapax legomenon derived from the root 'alah ("go up"), referring to raising the hands in prayer and blessing.
native_notes.8:8: The Pual participle mephorash ("distinctly") can also mean "with translation" or "paragraph by paragraph" (cf. the cognate Aramaic participle in Ezra 4:18). The verb wayyavinu with bammiqra' is taken intransitively as "they understood what was read" (cf. v. 12), though it could also be parsed as a causative Hiphil meaning "they gave understanding of the reading."
native_notes.8:9: The title "the governor" renders the Persian loanword hattirshata', used of the governor of Judah (cf. Ezra 2:63; Neh 7:65, 70; 10:2).
native_notes.8:10: The noun ma'oz ("stronghold") denotes a fortified refuge or place of strength.
native_notes.9:5: In the Masoretic Text, the Levites' call to worship shifts directly to second-person prayer to God in the second half of this verse and continues through v. 37 without naming a new speaker (unlike the Septuagint, which inserts Ezra before v. 6).
native_notes.9:6: Ketiv reads 't (a rare defective spelling of the second-person masculine singular pronoun); Qere reads 'attah ("You"), which is followed here.
native_notes.9:17: Ketiv reads wchsd (with an extra conjunction waw); Qere reads chesed, forming werav-chesed ("and abounding in loyal love"), which is followed here. In addition, the Masoretic Text reads bemiryam ("in their rebellion"), whereas some ancient versions harmonize to "in Egypt."
native_notes.9:22: The clause "apportioned them to every boundary" (literally "apportioned them to a corner/border") idiomatically refers to dividing and allotting territories to every district. The Masoretic Text then repeats "the land" epexegetically ("the land of Sihon, even the land of the king of Heshbon").
native_notes.9:32: The particle 'et here introduces the grammatical subject ("all the hardship"), a syntactic usage attested in Late Biblical Hebrew (similarly in vv. 19 and 34).
native_notes.10:2: The phrase on the sealed documents translates the masculine plural Qal passive participle hachatumim, paralleling the singular hechatum in 10:1 and indicating either the sealed documents or those who set their seals. Governor translates hattirshata, a Persian administrative title.
native_notes.10:20: Translates the qere Nebai; the ketiv reads Nobai.
native_notes.10:30: Join firmly translates the Hiphil participle machaziqim with the preposition al, literally holding fast upon, expressing firm solidarity in taking the covenant oath.
native_notes.10:32: The Hebrew literally reads we will leave off the seventh year and the exaction of every hand, referring to letting the land lie fallow in the sabbatical year and canceling every creditor's claim.
native_notes.10:39: When the Levites collect the tithes translates the syncopated Hiphil infinitive construct baaser, matching the Piel participle measserim in 10:38; both stems here denote collecting the tithes.
native_notes.11:14: Haggedolim is a Hebrew plural form meaning the great ones, here treated as a family or ancestral name; it may alternatively be rendered the son of the great men.
native_notes.11:17: Translates the qere Jeduthun; the ketiv reads Jedithun. The phrase leader to start giving thanks in prayer renders the Masoretic Hebrew rosh hattechillah yehodeh lattephillah, literally head of the beginning, he gives thanks for the prayer, with the Hiphil imperfect yehodeh retaining its he.
native_notes.11:24: At the king's hand translates the Hebrew idiom leyad hammelek, denoting service as the king's advisor or liaison.
native_notes.11:25: Dependent towns here and in 11:27, 30, and 31 translates Hebrew banot, literally daughters, denoting satellite towns attached to a mother city, in distinction from chatserim, unwalled villages.
native_notes.11:35: The Hebrew phrase "the Valley of the Craftsmen" may either name a third settlement or describe the valley of Lod and Ono.
native_notes.11:36: The Hebrew is a terse verbless clause literally reading And from the Levites, divisions of Judah for Benjamin, indicating that certain Levitical divisions from Judah were assigned to Benjamin's territory.
native_notes.12:14: The translation follows the Qere (read form) Melichu; the Ketiv (written form) reads Malluchi (compare Malluch in 12:2).
native_notes.12:16: The translation follows the Qere (read form) Iddo; the Ketiv (written form) reads Adaiah (or Iddia).
native_notes.12:17: In the Masoretic Text, no personal name follows for Miniamin; the phrase carries a disjunctive accent directly before for Moadiah, Piltai, indicating an apparent omission in the Hebrew text.
native_notes.12:31: Hebrew todot literally means thanksgivings, here denoting choirs giving thanks, and tahalukot is a rare noun meaning processions found only here. The words One went are implied by the contrast with the second thanksgiving choir in 12:38.
native_notes.12:46: The translation follows the Qere (read form), plural construct heads of the singers; the Ketiv (written form) reads singular head of the singers.
native_notes.13:13: The verb wa'otserah is a rare denominative Hiphil of 'atsar (from 'otsar, storehouse/treasury), meaning appointed as treasurers, forming a wordplay with 'otsarot (storehouses).
native_notes.13:19: The Qal verb tsalelu (from tsalal, related to tsel, shadow) occurs only here in the Hebrew Bible in the sense of growing dark or falling into shadow, with the gates of Jerusalem as its grammatical subject.
native_notes.13:23: Ketiv writes the plene forms for Ashdodite and Ammonite while Qere reads the defective forms with no difference in meaning. The Hiphil verb hoshivu (from yashav, literally caused to dwell) is a Late Biblical Hebrew idiom used here and in 13:27 for marrying foreign women.
native_notes.13:25: Literally "if you give... and if you take," a standard Hebrew elliptical oath formula after the Hiphil verb of swearing (wa'ashbi'em) expressing an emphatic negative prohibition.
native_notes.13:27: The form hanishma' can be parsed as Qal imperfect 1cp ("should we listen" or "do we hear") or identically vocalized Niphal perfect 3ms ("has it been heard"), yielding either "should we listen to you" or "must we hear concerning you."
